akhfash:13-13.t:
He said ﴿مَّا لَكُمْ لاَ تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَاراً﴾, that is: you do not fear Allah's grandeur. "الرَّجاء" here is fear, and "الوَقار" is grandeur. The poet said [in the ṭawīl metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-second verse cited as evidence]:
إِذَا لَسَعَتْهُ النَحْلُ لَمْ يَرْجُ لَسْعَهَا * [وخَالَفَها في بَيْتِ نوبٍ عَواسِلِ]
(When the bees sting him he does not fear their sting, and he comes at them in the home of honey-making swarms.)

akhfash:14-14.t: And He said ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَاراً﴾: at one stage a clinging clot (عَلَقَة) and at another stage a lump of flesh (مُضْغَة).

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿وَجَعَلَ ٱلْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُوراً﴾: this is only — and Allah knows best — in accordance with the speech of the Arabs, for the moon is only in the lowest heaven, according to what has been mentioned; just as you say "أَتَيْتُ بني تَمِيم" ("I came to Banū Tamīm") when you only came to some of them.

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿وَٱللَّهُ أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ ٱلأَرْضِ نَبَاتاً﴾: He made "النَّبَات" the maṣdar (verbal noun), whereas the maṣdar is "الإِنْبات", because this indicates the meaning.

akhfash:20-20.t: And He said ﴿سُبُلاً فِجَاجاً﴾: its singular is "الفَجُّ", which is the road.

akhfash:24-24.t: And He said ﴿وَلاَ تَزِدِ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾ because this is from the words of Noah, an imprecation against them.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِ أَنْ أَنْذِرْ﴾ i.e. with warning ﴿قَوْمَكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ﴾ if they do not believe ﴿عَذَابٌ أَلِيمٌ﴾ painful, in this world and the Hereafter.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿قَالَ يَا قَوْمِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear in warning,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿أَنِ﴾ i.e. that I say to you: ﴿اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ مِنْ is redundant (zāʾida), since by Islam what came before it is forgiven; or it is partitive, to exclude the rights of [Allah's] servants. ﴿وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ﴾ without punishment ﴿إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى﴾ the term of death. ﴿إِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ﴾ for your punishment if you do not believe ﴿إِذَا جَاءَ لَا يُؤَخَّرُ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ that, you would have believed.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِي لَيْلًا وَنَهَارًا﴾ i.e. constantly, without break,

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعَائِي إِلَّا فِرَارًا﴾ from faith.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِنِّي كُلَّمَا دَعَوْتُهُمْ لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ جَعَلُوا أَصَابِعَهُمْ فِي آذَانِهِمْ﴾ so as not to hear my words ﴿وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيَابَهُمْ﴾ covered their heads with them so as not to look at me ﴿وَأَصَرُّوا﴾ on their unbelief ﴿وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ were too proud for faith ﴿اسْتِكْبَارًا﴾

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهَارًا﴾ i.e. at the top of my voice,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنِّي أَعْلَنْتُ لَهُمْ﴾ my voice ﴿وَأَسْرَرْتُ﴾ the speech ﴿لَهُمْ إِسْرَارًا﴾

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ﴾ from idolatry; ﴿إِنَّهُ كَانَ غَفَّارًا﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿يُرْسِلِ السَّمَاءَ﴾ the rain — and they had been deprived of it — ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْرَارًا﴾ pouring abundantly,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ orchards ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ أَنْهَارًا﴾ flowing.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿مَا لَكُمْ لَا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَارًا﴾ i.e. [do not] hope for Allah's honouring of you by your believing,

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَارًا﴾ plural of طَوْر, which is a state: one stage a sperm-drop, one stage a clinging clot, up to the completion of the human being's creation; and reflecting on his creation obliges faith in his Creator.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَوْا﴾ look ﴿كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا﴾ some above others,

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ﴾ i.e. in their totality, which is true of the lowest heaven, ﴿نُورًا وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِرَاجًا﴾ a shining lamp, and it is stronger than the light of the moon.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ﴾ created you ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ since He created your father Adam from it ﴿نَبَاتًا﴾

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا﴾ buried ﴿وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ﴾ for the resurrection ﴿إِخْرَاجًا﴾

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًا﴾ spread out,

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿قَالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي وَاتَّبَعُوا﴾ i.e. the lowly and the poor ﴿مَنْ لَمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُ وَوُلْدُهُ﴾ — and they are the chiefs who were blessed with that; وُلْد is read with ḍamma on the wāw and sukūn on the lām, and with fatḥa on both [وَوَلَدُهُ]; the first is said to be the plural of وَلَد with fatḥa on both, like خَشَب and خُشْب, and is also said to have the same meaning, like بُخْل and بَخَل — ﴿إِلَّا خَسَارًا﴾ tyranny and unbelief,

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَمَكَرُوا﴾ i.e. the chiefs ﴿مَكْرًا كُبَّارًا﴾ very great, by denying Noah and harming him and those who followed him,

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ to the lowly: ﴿لَا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا﴾ with fatḥa on the wāw and with ḍamma ﴿وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا﴾ these are the names of their idols.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا﴾ by them ﴿كَثِيرًا﴾ of people, by commanding them to worship them. ﴿وَلَا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَالًا﴾ conjoined to قَدْ أَضَلُّوا; he prayed against them when it was revealed to him: "None of your people will believe except those who have already believed."

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿مِمَّا﴾ the mā is a connective (ṣila) ﴿خَطَايَاهُمْ﴾ — in one reading [خَطِيئَاتِهِمْ] with the hamza — ﴿أُغْرِقُوا﴾ by the Flood ﴿فَأُدْخِلُوا نَارًا﴾ they were punished with it straight after the drowning, beneath the water, ﴿فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ﴾ i.e. other than ﴿اللَّهِ أَنْصَارًا﴾ to ward off the punishment from them.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ دَيَّارًا﴾ i.e. a dweller in a home; the meaning is: anyone.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوا إِلَّا فَاجِرًا كَفَّارًا﴾ one who sins and disbelieves. He said that because of the revelation to him mentioned above.

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ﴾ and they were both believers ﴿وَلِمَنْ دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ﴾ my dwelling or my place of worship ﴿مُؤْمِنًا وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾ until the Day of Resurrection ﴿وَلَا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا تَبَارًا﴾ destruction; and so they were destroyed.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿نُوحاً﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿إِلى قَوْمِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿أَنْ أَنْذِرْ﴾ an explicative particle (ḥarf tafsīr), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿قَوْمَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and its mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿يا﴾ a vocative particle. ﴿قَوْمِ إِنِّي﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the omitted yāʾ of the first person, and the vocative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and inna and its noun. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿نَذِيرٌ﴾ khabar of inna. ﴿مُبِينٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the nominal clause is the object of the saying.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an is an explicative particle (ḥarf tafsīr), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the Name of Majesty is its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is explicative (mufassira), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to اعبدوا.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿يَغْفِرْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the response to the request, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb, and they function as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿إِلى أَجَلٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مُسَمًّى﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿إِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ﴾ inna and its noun, annexed to the Name of Majesty. ﴿إِذا جاءَ﴾ idhā is a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿لا يُؤَخَّرُ﴾ negative, and a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; idhā together with its protasis and apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle that does not make jussive. ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of كنتم, and the clause «كنتم..» is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:5-6.t: ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for lightness; the vocative clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿قَوْمِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿لَيْلًا﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿وَنَهاراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ليلا. ﴿فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the hāʾ is its first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿دُعائِي﴾ a postponed fāʿil. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿فِراراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِنِّي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and inna and its noun. ﴿كُلَّما دَعَوْتُهُمْ﴾ kullamā is a conditional particle that does not make jussive, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿لِتَغْفِرَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb تغفر. ﴿جَعَلُوا أَصابِعَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي آذانِهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb, and they stand in the place of the second object; the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاسْتَغْشَوْا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جعلوا. ﴿ثِيابَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَأَصَرُّوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ conjoined to استغشوا. ﴿اسْتِكْباراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

daas-irab:8-9.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُهُمْ﴾ thumma is a conjunction, and inna and its noun, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿جِهاراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿إِنِّي أَعْلَنْتُ﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ﴾ conjoined to أعلنت لهم. ﴿إِسْراراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq.

daas-irab:10-11.t: ﴿فَقُلْتُ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿اسْتَغْفِرُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿رَبَّكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ inna [and] its noun. ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and its noun is latent (mustatir). ﴿غَفَّاراً﴾ khabar (predicate) of kāna; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position. ﴿يُرْسِلِ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿السَّماءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِدْراراً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the response to the request, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يرسل, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِأَمْوالٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَبَنِينَ﴾ conjoined to أموال. ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿جَنَّاتٍ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ أَنْهاراً﴾ parsed like the preceding one.

daas-irab:13-14.t: ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لا تَرْجُونَ﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَقاراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl. ﴿قَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ﴾ a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَطْواراً﴾ ḥāl; the clause is a ḥāl clause.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَوْا﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun as ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿سَماواتٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿طِباقاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of سبع; the clause خلق stands in place of the two objects of تروا.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿وَجَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الْقَمَرَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿نُوراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it, and what follows it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:17-18.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject), and a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿مِنَ الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿نَباتاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ﴾ thumma is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ﴾ conjoined to يعيدكم. ﴿إِخْراجاً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq.

daas-irab:19-20.t: ﴿وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ (subject), and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِساطاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لِتَسْلُكُوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl), and the wāw is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to جعل. ﴿مِنْها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿سُبُلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِجاجاً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); فجاجا means wide.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿قالَ نُوحٌ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿رَبِّ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for lightness. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the vocative clause with what follows it is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَاتَّبَعُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لَمْ يَزِدْهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مالُهُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَوَلَدُهُ﴾ conjoined to ماله. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿خَساراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وَمَكَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مَكْراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿كُبَّاراً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿لا تَذَرُنَّ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil, and the nūn is for emphasis. ﴿آلِهَتَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلا تَذَرُنَّ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَدًّا﴾ mafʿūl bihi, and what follows it is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿وَقَدْ﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا﴾ qad is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿كَثِيراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَلا تَزِدِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lā, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿ضَلالًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿مِمَّا﴾ min is a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ redundant (zāʾida). ﴿خَطِيئاتِهِمْ﴾ genitive (majrūr) by min, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿أُغْرِقُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَأُدْخِلُوا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أغرقوا. ﴿ناراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ من دون is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿أَنْصاراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿وَقالَ نُوحٌ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿رَبِّ لا تَذَرْ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for lightness, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lā, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَى الْأَرْضِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿دَيَّاراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the vocative clause and the verbal clause are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّكَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ﴾ in is a conditional particle that makes jussive, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿يُضِلُّوا﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عِبادَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the apodosis, with no grammatical position, and the condition and its apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of إنك, and the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلا يَلِدُوا﴾ lā is negative, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿فاجِراً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَفَّاراً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿رَبِّ اغْفِرْ﴾ the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, omitted for lightness, and a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ) whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿لِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَلِوالِدَيَّ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to لي. ﴿وَلِمَنْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also conjoined [to it]. ﴿دَخَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿بَيْتِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مُؤْمِناً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا تَزِدِ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lā, whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿تَباراً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

dervis-irab:1-9.t:
* Vocabulary:
(وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ) and they covered themselves with them, as though they sought that their garments should cover them, or that [the garments] should cover them, so that they would not see him, out of aversion to looking at one who counsels them about the religion of Allah.

* I'rab:
(إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنا نُوحاً إِلى قَوْمِهِ) Inna and its noun, and the clause أرسلنا is its khabar (predicate); نوحا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) and إلى قومه is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أرسلنا. (أَنْ أَنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ) An may be maṣdariyya, so together with what it governs it is an interpreted maṣdar, accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to أرسلنا; the meaning is: We sent him by saying to him "Warn". It may also be explicative, because sending contains the meaning of saying. أنذر is an imperative verb and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anta"; قومك is the direct object; من قبل is attached to أنذر. An and what falls in its scope is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the genitive by construct; يأتيهم is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the hāʾ is the direct object; عذاب is the agent and أليم an adjective (naʿt). (قالَ يا قَوْمِ إِنِّي لَكُمْ نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ) قال is a past verb and its agent is latent, its implied form being "huwa"; يا is a vocative particle and قوم is the one addressed (munādā), in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the first person; the discussion of the munādā in construct with the first-person yāʾ has preceded. Inna and its noun; لكم is attached to نذير; نذير is the khabar and مبين an adjective. (أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ) An is maṣdariyya or explicative; the discussion of it has just preceded. اعبدوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; الله is the direct object; اتقوه and أطيعون are conjoined to اعبدوا. The first-person yāʾ was dropped to match the verse-endings, i.e. وأطيعوني. (يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى) يغفر is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer of the command; لكم is attached to يغفر; من ذنوبكم is in the position of the accusative as the object of يغفر, because min is partitive, i.e. some of your sins, since faith wipes out the sins before it, not those after it. It is said it is for the beginning of the extent, and it is said it is redundant (zāʾida); this is the school of al-Akhfash, because he permits its redundancy in affirmative and other contexts, whereas the Basrans and most of the Kufans stipulate for its redundancy that it be preceded by a negation, a prohibition or a question, and that it come before an indefinite noun. يؤخركم is conjoined to يغفر and the kāf is the direct object; إلى أجل is attached to يؤخركم and مسمى is an adjective of أجل. We shall present an interesting discussion about this postponement of the punishment in the section on benefits. (إِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ إِذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ) The clause gives the reason for what preceded. Inna and its noun; إذا is an adverb for future time, putting its condition in the genitive, attached to its apodosis; the clause جاء is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being put in construct with it; the clause لا يؤخر has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition that does not cause the jussive. Law is conditional; كنتم is kāna and its noun, and the clause تعلمون is its khabar. The apodosis of law is omitted, just as the object of تعلمون is omitted, i.e. if you knew that, you would believe. (قالَ: رَبِّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ قَوْمِي لَيْلًا وَنَهاراً) ربّ is a munādā in construct with the omitted first-person yāʾ, and the vocative particle is omitted. Inna and its noun, and the clause دعوت is its khabar; قومي is the direct object; ليلا and نهارا are two adverbs attached to دعوت. The clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (فَلَمْ يَزِدْهُمْ دُعائِي إِلَّا فِراراً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; lam is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and the jussive; يزدهم is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lam, and the hāʾ is the first direct object; دعائي is the agent; إلا is a particle of restriction and فرارا is the second direct object; the exception is emptied (mufarragh). (وَإِنِّي كُلَّما دَعَوْتُهُمْ لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ جَعَلُوا أَصابِعَهُمْ فِي آذانِهِمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; inna and its noun; كلما is an adverb attached to جعلوا, with mā being maṣdariyya or an indefinite noun. دعوتهم is a verb, its agent and its direct object; the lām is causal, and تغفر is an imperfect verb in the accusative by an, optionally implied after the causal lām; the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to دعوتهم. The clause جعلوا has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a condition that does not cause the jussive, namely كلما. أصابعهم is the first object of جعلوا and في آذانهم is in the place of the second object. (وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ وَأَصَرُّوا وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا اسْتِكْباراً) استغشوا is conjoined to جعلوا and ثيابهم is the direct object; أصرّوا and استكبروا are also conjoined; استكبارا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (ثُمَّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهاراً) ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; inna and its noun, and the clause دعوتهم is its khabar; جهارا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq, being a maṣdar from the meaning [of the verb], because calling may be open or otherwise, so it is of the type رجع القهقرى ("he went back backwards") and قعد القرفصاء ("he sat squatting"). It may also be a maṣdar in place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. openly and in an open manner, and making it the maṣdar itself is hyperbole. (ثُمَّ إِنِّي أَعْلَنْتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْراراً) conjoined to what preceded; إسرارا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «واستغشوا ثيابهم» there is a metonymy (kināya) for the extremity of their turning away from what he called them to: they are like someone who has blocked his hearing and covered his sight so as not to hear and see. One says, "So-and-so put on the garments of enmity". It is also said that the expression is literal, and the meaning of استغشوا ثيابهم is that they covered their faces with them so as not to see me, or put their garments over their heads so as not to hear my speech; on this view, covering with the garments is an addition to blocking the ears.
In the delay [expressed by thumma] and the repetition of the call there is clarification and emphasis. In this connection we quote the wording of al-Zamakhsharī because of its excellence. He said: «If you say: He mentioned that he called them by night and by day, then called them openly, then called them in secret and in public; so these must be three different calls for the conjunction to be valid — I say: He, upon him be blessing and peace, did as one who commands the right and forbids the wrong does, beginning with the lightest and rising to the more severe and then the more severe still. He began with counselling in secret; when they did not accept, he followed with openness as the second step; when that had no effect, he made the third step combining secrecy and openness. The meaning of thumma is to indicate the remoteness of the states from one another, because openness is harsher than secrecy, and combining the two matters is harsher than doing one of them alone». This is splendid speech whose depth few can fathom: it is known from His words ثم إني دعوتهم جهارا that the preceding call was in secret, so the thumma conveyed the disparity between openness and the preceding secrecy, and the second thumma conveyed that combining the two is harsher than each of them alone.

* Benefits:
Now, we promised you to present an enjoyable discussion that arose among the great exegetes about His words ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: How did He say ويؤخركم while informing that the postponement of the term is impossible, and is this anything but a contradiction? I say: Allah decreed, for example, that if the people of Noah believed He would let them live a thousand years, and if they remained in their disbelief He would destroy them at the end of nine hundred. So it was said to them: Believe, and He will postpone you to a named term, i.e. to a time that Allah has named and set as a limit which you reach and do not exceed, and that is the longer time, the completion of the thousand. Then He informed that when that term, the limit, comes, it is not postponed as this [other] time is postponed, and you would have no recourse; so hasten in the times of respite and postponement».
Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى is among what the Muʿtazila clung to in their saying that a person has two terms. They said: If it were one fixed term, then neither postponement would be valid if the limit had been reached, nor hastening [Translator's note: the source has «المعالجة», apparently for «المعاجلة», "hastening"] if it had not been reached». He said: «They have no hold in the verse, because the meaning is that Noah, upon him be peace, did not know whether they were among those who would be postponed or those who would be hastened [to punishment], nor did he say to them that you will be postponed beyond a term that has arrived for you. Rather, it was preordained from eternity that they were either among those for whom faith and postponement were decreed, or among those for whom disbelief and hastening were decreed. Then this meaning was strengthened and made apparent by His words: إن أجل الله إذا جاء لا يؤخر».
Al-Suyūṭī cleared away the obscurity that encroached on this expression by saying in his enjoyable commentary: «and He will postpone you without punishment», i.e. in this world; so it does not conflict with His words إن أجل الله إذا جاء لا يؤخر, because what is negated there as being postponed is the term itself, so there is no conflict between these two places.
The wording of al-Karkhī in his gloss on the Jalālayn: «His words "and He will postpone you without punishment" answer [the question]: how did He say ويؤخركم إلى أجل مسمى in addressing the people of Noah? For if what is meant is postponing them beyond the term decreed from eternity, that is impossible because of His words, the Exalted: ولن يؤخّر الله نفسا إذا جاء أجلها; or [if it is] postponing them until the coming of their decreed term, as with others, whether they believe or not, [then it has no point]. [Translator's note: the bracketed completion is added for clarity; the source sentence is elliptical.] Its clarification is that its meaning is: He will postpone the punishment from you until the end of your terms, on the supposition of faith, so He will not punish you in this world if a sin occurs from you, as He punished other disbelieving nations in it».

dervis-irab:10-20.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مِدْراراً) pouring abundantly; masculine and feminine are the same in it, and this sameness holds regularly in the pattern mifʿāl, a form of intensification.
(أَطْواراً) plural of ṭawr, which is the state and the time (tāra). In al-Miṣbāḥ: «al-ṭawr, with fatḥa, is a time: "he did that ṭawran after ṭawr", i.e. time after time. Al-ṭawr is also the state and the form; the plural is aṭwār, like thawb and athwāb. "He overstepped his ṭawr", i.e. the state befitting him».
(فِجاجاً) wide; plural of fajj, which is the wide road; it is said it is the passage between two mountains.

* I'rab:
(فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قلت is a verb and its agent; استغفروا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); ربكم is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). Inna and its noun, and the clause كان is its khabar (predicate); the noun of kāna is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa", and غفارا is its khabar. The clause استغفروا is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause إنه كان غفارا has no grammatical position because it gives the reason for seeking forgiveness. In al-Shihāb: «What is meant by seeking forgiveness is not merely saying "I seek Allah's forgiveness", but turning back from sins and purifying tongues and hearts». (يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْراراً) يرسل is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer of the command; the agent is latent, referring to Allah the Exalted; السماء is the direct object; عليكم is attached to (mutaʿalliq) يرسل; مدرارا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from السماء. (وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ جَنَّاتٍ وَيَجْعَلْ لَكُمْ أَنْهاراً) يمددكم is conjoined to يرسل and the kāf is the direct object; بأموال is attached to يمددكم and بنين is conjoined to أموال; يجعل is an imperfect verb in the jussive, conjoined to يمددكم; لكم is in the place of the second object and جنات is the direct object; ويجعل لكم أنهارا is conjoined to the previous clause. What is meant by جنات is the orchards of this world. (ما لَكُمْ لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقاراً) ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and لكم is the khabar; lā is negative and ترجون is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; the clause لا ترجون is a ḥāl from the kāf in لكم. لله is a ḥāl, because the lām is for clarification; had it come later it would have been an adjective of الوقار. وقارا is the direct object of ترجون, i.e. reverence and veneration. Further clarification of this expression will come in the section on benefits. (وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْواراً) The wāw is circumstantial; qad is a particle of realisation; خلقكم is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; the clause is a ḥāl from the agent of ترجون. أطوارا is a ḥāl interpreted as a derived word, i.e. passing from state to state. (أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقاً) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval; lam is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and the jussive; تروا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lam, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent. The seeing is cognitive, i.e. have you not taken heed and reflected? كيف is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl, governed by خلق. خلق الله is a past verb and its agent, and the clause stands in place of the two objects of تروا, which is suspended from governing by the interrogative. سبع سموات is the direct object, and طباقا is an adjective of سبع, i.e. one above another; or it is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "they were made in layers (ṭubbiqat ṭibāqan)", so it would be the maṣdar of طابقت مطابقة وطباقا. That was mentioned in Sūrat al-Mulk. (وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُوراً وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِراجاً) The wāw is a conjunction; جعل القمر is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; فيهن is a ḥāl and نورا is the second direct object; وجعل الشمس سراجا is conjoined to the previous clause. (وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَباتاً) The wāw is a conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause أنبتكم is the khabar; من الأرض is attached to أنبتكم; نباتا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). It may be a maṣdar of أنبت with the additional letters dropped, and this is called a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar); or it may be the maṣdar of an implied نبتم, i.e. "and you grew a growing", so it is accusative by the implied reflexive verb (al-muṭāwiʿ). The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «The meaning is: He caused you to grow and you grew a growing; or it is accusative by أنبتكم because it contains the meaning of نبتم». (ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيها وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْراجاً) conjoined to what preceded. (وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ بِساطاً) The wāw is a conjunction; الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause جعل is the khabar; لكم is a ḥāl; الأرض is the first direct object and بساطا the second direct object. (لِتَسْلُكُوا مِنْها سُبُلًا فِجاجاً) The lām is the lām of cause; تسلكوا is an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the causal lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to جعل. منها is a ḥāl from سبلا, i.e. being from the earth; had it come later it would have been an adjective of it. سبلا is the direct object and فجاجا an adjective.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «يرسل السماء عليكم مدرارا» there is a synecdoche-type metaphor (majāz mursal) whose relation is that of place: by السماء He meant the rain, because rain comes down from it. A poet said:
إذا نزل السماء بأرض قوم ... رعيناه وإن كانوا غضابا
(When the sky [i.e. rain] comes down on a people's land, we graze it, even if they are angry.)
What is meant by the verse is describing their courage: if they dare to graze the plants of angry people, they are all the more likely to dare against others. In the verse there is also istikhdām (using a word in one sense and its pronoun in another): he used السماء and returned the pronoun to it with the meaning of plants, because it is their cause.
2- In His words «والله أنبتكم من الأرض نباتا» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), because He likened them to plants: He borrowed "causing to grow" for "bringing into being", as one says "May Allah plant you for good". This metaphor had a benefit, because it indicated origination in time: if they are plants, they are inevitably originated, as plants are originated. Because of this the Ḥashwiyya were called "al-Nābitiyya" and "al-Nawābit" (the sprouts), on account of the newness of their school in Islam.

* Benefits:
The sayings of the exegetes differed concerning His words «ما لكم لا ترجون لله وقارا». We present here extracts from their sayings and then follow them with what clears up their obscurity. Al-rajāʾ means hope and fear. Abū ʿUbayda said: «لا ترجون: you do not fear». They said: al-waqār means greatness and authority, so the speech is a threat and an intimidation. The wording of al-Zamakhsharī: «The meaning is: what is the matter with you that you are not in a state in which you hope for Allah's honouring you in the abode of reward? لله clarifies the one who is honoured; had it come later it would have been a complement (ṣila) of الوقار … Or: you do not fear Allah's forbearance and His refraining from hastening the punishment, so that you might believe. It is said: what is the matter with you that you do not fear the greatness of Allah? And from Ibn ʿAbbās: you do not fear an outcome from Allah, because the outcome is the state in which matters settle and reward and punishment become fixed, from وقر when it became fixed and settled». The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «It is said: what is the matter with you that you do not make your hope in Allah and your encounter with Him a sedateness (waqār)? On this view it would be from them, as though He says: deliberation on your part and steadiness in reflection, because thought is a likely place of levity, rashness and obstinacy». Quṭrub said: This is a Ḥijāzī dialect; Hudhayl, Khuzāʿa and Muḍar say لم أرجُ meaning "I did not care".
The wording of Abū al-Suʿūd: «ما لكم لا ترجون لله وقارا is a disapproval of their having any reason at all for their not believing in a greatness for Allah the Exalted, on the basis that al-rajāʾ means belief. لا ترجون is a ḥāl from the pronoun of those addressed, and what governs it is the meaning of being settled in لكم. لله is attached to an implied element that occurs as a ḥāl from وقارا; had it come later it would have been an adjective of it. That is: what reason has come to you, while you do not believe in a greatness for Allah the Exalted that requires venerating Him by believing in Him and obeying Him, وقد خلقكم أطوارا, i.e. while you are in a state wholly at odds with what you are doing, namely that you know that He, the Exalted, created you at one stage as elements, then as nourishment, then as humours, then as drops of fluid, then as clinging clots, then as lumps of flesh, then as bones and flesh, then brought you into being as another creation. For falling short in revering one whose affairs are such, in overpowering might and perfect beneficence, while knowing them, is something that hardly issues from a rational being».
What we derive from all this is that the people went to extremes in despising him, upon him be peace, mocking him and making jokes about him; so Allah commanded them to adhere earnestly to revering and respecting him and to turn away from this unbecoming treatment. That is: if you revere Noah and abandon belittling him and making jokes about him, that will be obedience to Allah, drawing near to Him and compliance with His commands; so what is the matter with you that you do not seize this opportunity and attain the pleasure of Allah by revering and respecting him?

dervis-irab:21-28.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كُبَّاراً) with ḍamma on the kāf and doubling of the bāʾ; it is a form of intensification more intense than كُبار, with ḍamma and without doubling. (ود، سواع، يَغُوثَ، يَعُوقَ، نسر) names of idols they used to worship.
(دَيَّاراً) Al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is one of the nouns used in general negation. One says ما بالدار ديّار and ديّور, like قيّام and قيّوم. It is a fayʿāl from al-dawr or from al-dār, and its origin is دَيْوار, and what was done to the origin of سيّد and ميّت was done to it; had it been a faʿʿāl, it would have been دوّار». The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «ديّارا is one of the words of generality used in negation and what resembles it. Its pattern is fayʿāl; its origin is دَيْوار: the yāʾ and the wāw came together, the first of them having a sukūn, so they were assimilated». In al-Qāmūs: «ما به داريّ, ديّار, دوريّ and ديّور: [there is not in it] anyone».
(تَباراً) destruction.

* I'rab:
(قالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي) قال نوح is a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); رب is the one addressed (munādā), in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the first person; inna and its noun, and the clause عصوني is its khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). (وَاتَّبَعُوا مَنْ لَمْ يَزِدْهُ مالُهُ وَوَلَدُهُ إِلَّا خَساراً) اتبعوا is conjoined to عصوني; من is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); lam is a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and the jussive; يزده is an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the hāʾ is the direct object; ماله is the agent and ولده is conjoined to ماله; إلا is a particle of restriction and خسارا is the second direct object of يزده. (وَمَكَرُوا مَكْراً كُبَّاراً) The wāw is a conjunction; مكروا is a past verb and its agent; مكرا is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and كبارا is an adjective (naʿt) of مكرا, i.e. exceedingly great. (وَقالُوا لا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَلا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلا سُواعاً وَلا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْراً) The wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a past verb and its agent; lā is prohibitive and تذرن is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw [of the agent] is dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis; آلهتكم is the direct object. ولا تذرن is conjoined to the first لا تذرن, and ودّا and what is conjoined to it are the object of تذرن. يغوث and يعوق are diptotes because of being proper names together with the verbal pattern, if they are Arabic, or being proper names together with foreignness, if they are foreign. It was read ولا يغوثا ويعوقا, fully declined, for two reasons: first, that they were declined for harmony, since before them come two declined nouns and after them a declined noun; second, that it follows the dialect of those who decline the diptote absolutely, a dialect reported by al-Kisāʾī. (وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا كَثِيراً وَلا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلالًا) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause قد أضلوا is the object of an omitted saying, conjoined to the preceding قال, i.e. he said: "they have disobeyed me", and he said: "they have led astray". أضلوا is a verb and its agent and كثيرا is the direct object. The wāw conjoins to the omitted saying. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: To what is His word ولا تزد الظالمين conjoined? I say: To his word رب إنهم عصوني, by way of relating the speech of Noah, upon him be peace, after قال and after the wāw that stands in for it. Its meaning is: he said "My Lord, they have disobeyed me" and he said "Do not increase the wrongdoers except in error", i.e. he said these two sayings, and they are in the position of the accusative because they are the two objects of قال». Lā is prohibitive and تزد is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lā; الظالمين is an object; إلا is a particle of restriction and ضلالا is the direct object. The wording of Abū Ḥayyān: «ولا تزد is conjoined to قد أضلوا because it is related by an implied قال; harmony is not stipulated in conjoined clauses; rather, a statement may be conjoined to a request and vice versa, contrary to those who stipulated it». The wording of al-Shihāb al-Khafājī: «That is, لا تزد is a second saying of Noah, upon him be peace. Allah conjoined one of his two sayings to the other, and the wāw in it is from the speech of Allah the Exalted, not from the speech of Noah, because that would entail conjoining a performative (inshāʾ) to a statement (ikhbār). So Allah related one of his two sayings by heading it with the word قال, and related his other saying by conjoining it to his first saying with the wāw that stands in for the word قال». (مِمَّا خَطِيئاتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا فَأُدْخِلُوا ناراً) Min is a preposition and mā is redundant (zāʾida); خطيئاتهم is genitive (majrūr) by causal min, and the preposition and its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) أغرقوا; أغرقوا is a past passive verb. فأدخلوا is conjoined to أغرقوا; their entering the Fire was made to follow immediately upon their drowning in view of its nearness, and because it will inevitably be, so it is as though it had already been. نارا is the second direct object, by extension of usage. (فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْصاراً) also a conjoining with immediate succession; lam is a particle of negation, conversion and the jussive; يجدوا is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lam; لهم is in the place of the second object of يجدوا; من دون الله is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and أنصارا is the first object of يجدوا. (وَقالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ لا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ دَيَّاراً) The wāw is a conjunction; قال نوح is a past verb and its agent; رب is a munādā from which the vocative particle has been omitted, and it is in construct with the omitted first-person yāʾ. Lā is prohibitive and تذر is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lā; على الأرض is attached to تذر; من الكافرين is a ḥāl because it was originally an adjective of ديارا; ديارا is the object of تذر. (إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا عِبادَكَ وَلا يَلِدُوا إِلَّا فاجِراً كَفَّاراً) Inna and its noun, and the clause gives the reason for Noah's request, upon him be peace. If it is asked: How did he know that their children would be like them? It is answered that he remained among them a thousand years less fifty, so he fathomed their inner selves and sounded their depths: a man among them would go off with his son and say to him:
"Beware of this man, for he is a liar, and my father warned me against him"; then the old would die and the young would grow up upon what his father had taught and instilled in him before. In is conditional; تذرهم is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) and the hāʾ is the direct object; يضلوا is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of إنك. عبادك is the direct object. The wāw is a conjunction, lā is negative, and يلدوا is an imperfect verb conjoined to يضلوا, and the wāw is the agent; إلا is a particle of restriction, فاجرا is the object of يضلوا [Translator's note: so in the source; the governing verb of فاجرا is evidently يلدوا], and كفارا is an adjective. (رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوالِدَيَّ وَلِمَنْ دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِناً وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتِ) رب is a munādā in construct; its like has preceded. اغفر is a verb of supplication; لي is attached to اغفر; لوالدي is conjoined to لي and لمن is also conjoined; the clause دخل بيتي is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and مؤمنا is a ḥāl; للمؤمنين والمؤمنات is also conjoined. (وَلا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا تَباراً) The wāw is a conjunction; lā is prohibitive in supplication; تزد is an imperfect verb in the jussive by lā; الظالمين is the first direct object; إلا is a particle of restriction and تبارا is the second direct object; the exception is emptied (mufarragh). In al-Miṣbāḥ: «تبر يتبر, of the patterns of قتل and تعب, when he perished; it becomes transitive by doubling, so one says تبّره, and the noun is التبار. The faʿāl pattern, with fatḥa, often comes from faʿʿala, as in كلّم كلاما, سلّم سلاما and ودّع وداعا».

* Rhetoric:
In His words «ولا يلدوا إلا فاجرا كفّارا» there is a synecdoche-type metaphor (majāz mursal) whose relation is what [the thing] will become, because they will not be wicked at the time of birth but, in any case, a long time after it.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَنْ أَنذِرْ قَوْمَكَ﴾.
That is: We sent him with the warning. (أن) is in the position of the accusative, because you have dropped the preposition from it. Had it been إنا أرسلنا نوحا إلى قومه أنذر قومك, without أن, [it would have been correct], because "sending" is in origin a [kind of] saying; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is so, without أن.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾.
Years of hardship had pressed hard on them and carried off their wealth because the rain had ceased, and their women had stopped bearing children; so He said: ﴿وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾.

farraa:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿مَّا لَكُمْ لاَ تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وَقَاراً﴾. That is: you do not fear Allah's majesty.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَاراً﴾.
A drop of sperm, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then bone.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقاً﴾.
If you wish, you may make طباق [217/b] accusative by the verb, i.e.: He created them layered one upon another; and if you wish, you may make it an adjective (naʿt) of السبع, not by the verb. Had it been سبع سمواتٍ طباقٍ in the genitive, it would be a good way, as is read: "ثِيابُ سُنْدسٍ خُضْرٍ" and "خضرٌ".

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ ٱلْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُوراً﴾.
It is mentioned that the back of the sun lights up the heavens adjacent to it, and its face lights up for the people of the earth; and likewise the moon. The meaning is: He made the sun and the moon a light in the heavens and the earth.

farraa:20-21.t:
His saying: ﴿سُبُلاً فِجَاجاً﴾.
Paths; its singular is فج, and they are wide roads.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Hushaym told me, from Mughīra, from Ibrāhīm, that he read: ﴿مَالُهُ وَوَلَدُهُ﴾.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَكَرُواْ مَكْراً كُبَّاراً﴾.
الكُبَّار means الكبير (great); and the Arabs say كُبَار.
They say: رجل حُسَّان جُمَّال (a very handsome, very beautiful man) with doubling, and حُسَان جُمَال light, in many of its like.

farraa:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَذَرُنَّ وَدّاً وَلاَ سُوَاعاً﴾.
These are gods that Iblīs made for them. The readers differed over ودّ: the people of Medina read (وُدًّا) with ḍamma, and al-Aʿmash and ʿĀṣim read (وَدًّا) with fatḥa.
They did not make (يَغُوثَ، ويَعُوقَ) fully declinable (lam yujrū), because they have an added yāʾ. Any proper noun that has [an added] yāʾ, tāʾ or alif is not made fully declinable; among them: يَملِك, يزيد, يعمَر, تغلب and أحمد. These are not made declinable because of what is added in them. Had they been made declinable because of their frequent use as names, it would be correct; and had they been made declinable as if intended as indefinite, that too would be correct.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "ولا تَذَرُنَّ وَدَّا ولا سُواعاً ويَغوثاً ويَعَوقاً ونَسْراً", with alif [i.e. with tanwīn]. ﴿وقَدْ أَضَلُّوا كثيرا﴾: He is saying: many people have gone astray through these idols. Had it been said: وقد أضلّت كثيرا or أضللن, it would be correct.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿مِّمَّا خَطِيۤئَاتِهِمْ﴾.
The Arabs make (ما) a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant) in what is intended in the manner of a conditional (jazāʾ), as if you said: إن خطيئاتهم ما أغرقوا (it was because of their sins that they were drowned); and that is how I saw it in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh, and its being put after is evidence of the conditional manner. Similar to it in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿أىَّ الأجَلَيْنِ ما قضيتُ فلا عُدْوانَ عَلَىّ﴾. Do you not see that you say: حيثما تكن أكن (wherever you are, I will be) and مهما تقل أقلْ (whatever you say, I will say)? Of that is: ﴿أَيًّا مَّا تَدْعُو فَلَه الأَسْماءُ الحسنى﴾: the conditional is joined with ما. But when it is a question they do not join it with ما; they say: كيف تصنع؟ (how do you act?) and أين تذهب؟ (where are you going?). When it is a question it is not joined with ما; when it is a conditional, it is joined, and joining is also omitted.
[Translator's note: «إن خطيئاتهم ما أغرقوا» is as printed; the expected illustrative form is «من خطيئاتهم ما أغرقوا».]

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿دَيَّاراً﴾.
It is from دُرت (I went round), but it is [on the pattern] fayʿāl from الدوران, just as ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb read: ﴿اللهُ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ هُوَ الْحَىُّ الْقَيّامُ﴾, which is from قمتُ.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾.
[A term] named among you, which you know: He will not cause you to die by drowning, burning or killing. There is no proof in this for the Qadarites, because He only meant: named among you. Similar to it: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِى يَبْدَأُ الْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عليه﴾: [easier] in your estimation, according to your knowledge.
His saying: ﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾.
من can be for the whole of what it applies to, or for part of it. As for "part", it is your saying: اشتريت من عبيدك (I bought some of your slaves); as for "the whole", it is your saying: رَوِيت من مائك (I quenched my thirst from your water). When it is in a position of totality, it is as if من were عن, as you say: اشتكيت من ماء شربته and عن ماء شربته (I fell ill from water I drank). It is as if in speech it were: يغفر لكم عن أذنابكم and من أذنابكم.
[Translator's note: «أذنابكم» is as printed (twice), evidently for «ذنوبكم» ("your sins").]

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿لَيْلاً وَنَهَاراً﴾.
That is: I called them in every way, secretly and openly.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿وَأَصَرُّواْ﴾.
That is: they kept silently to their polytheism, ﴿وَٱسْتَكْبَرُواْ﴾ [and were too proud] to believe.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The preposition phrase «إلى قومه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أرسلنا»; «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it explains the sending; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يأتيهم» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The clause «قال» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «نذير».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «أن» is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it is explanatory; «أطيعون» is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn; the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the implied (muqaddar) yāʾ is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «يغفر» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; the conditional clause «إذا جاء» is parenthetical, and its apodosis is omitted, the khabar (predicate) of «إن» indicating it; the clause «لو كنتم تعلمون» is resumptive, and the apodosis is omitted, i.e.: you would have hastened to what He commanded you.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: «ليلا» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «دعوت».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «فلم يَزِدْهم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ}; «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr), and «فرارًا» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: «كل» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعلوا»; «ما» is maṣdariyya and temporal, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «جعلوا» is the khabar (predicate) of «إني»; it is permissible for the khabar clause to lack a pronoun referring back to the speaker because it is linked to the clause «دعوتهم» by something resembling a condition, and the referring pronoun is explicit in it; the clause «دعوتهم» is the ṣila of the relative particle (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī); the preposition phrase «في آذانهم» is attached to the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «جِهَارًا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), being its kind.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «فقلت» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أسررت», and the clause «إنه كان» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «يرسل» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition; «مدرارا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السماء», and it is not made feminine because it is on the pattern mifʿāl.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «ما لكم»: [«ما»] is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); «لكم» is a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate); the clause «لا ترجون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the preposition phrase «لله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl from «وقارا».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «وقد خلقكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of {تَرْجُونَ}; «أطوارا» is a ḥāl from the kāf.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «كيف» is an interrogative noun, a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «خلق» is the object of the verb of seeing, suspended by the interrogative; «طباقًا» is a ḥāl from «سبع سماوات».

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The preposition phrase «فيهن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعل».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: «نباتًا» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), the maṣdar (verbal noun) being إنباتا.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The preposition phrase «لكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعل».

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: The preposition phrase «منها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تسلكوا»; «فجاجًا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «سبلا».

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «خسارًا» is the second object of «زاد», and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr).

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The clause «ومكروا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila (relative clause) of {مَنْ}; the pronoun is plural only by construing according to the meaning after construing according to the wording in {لَمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُ وَوَلَدُهُ}; «كُبَّارًا» is a naʿt (adjective) of intensification.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: (لا تذرن) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «لا» is prohibitive; the verb is an imperfect, jussive (majzūm) by the omission of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw of the plural, omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil (agent), and the nūn is for emphasis.

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The clause «وقد أضلُّوا» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied (muqaddar) saying, i.e.: Nūḥ said; this implied saying is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {قَالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي}; «كثيرًا» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «ولا تزد» is conjoined to «أضلوا»; «ضلالا» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The preposition phrase «ممَّا» is composed of the preposition «مِنْ» and the redundant «ما», and the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أغرقوا»; the preposition phrase «لهم» is attached to «يجدوا»; the preposition phrase «من دون» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أنصارًا».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The preposition phrase «من الكافرين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ديَّارا».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The conditional clause and its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) are the khabar (predicate) of «إن»; «كفارًا» is a naʿt (adjective) of «فاجرًا».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «مؤمنا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «دخل»; «تبارًا» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr).

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (أن أنذر قومك): (أن) has no position in i'rab; it is only for explanation, meaning (أي) "that is". It is also said that it is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by omission of the preposition, i.e. "with: warn". Its like in both aspects is (أن اعبدوا الله).

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (ليلا ونهارا): two adverbials of time (ẓarf zamān), and the governor of both is (دعوت).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t:
His saying (إلا فرارا): the second object of (يزدهم).
His saying (وإني كلما): (كلما) is accusative as an adverbial, and its governor is (جعلوا).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying (دعوتهم جهارا): (جهارا) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being open in calling them". It is also said the implied form is "possessing openness". It may also be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying (مدرارا): accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (السماء). The hāʾ [of the feminine] was not kept because the pattern mifʿāl for the feminine comes without hāʾ when it runs on the verb, as in (امرأة مذكار) "a woman who bears males", (مئناث) "who bears females" and (مطلاق) "often divorced".
His saying (سموات طباقا): it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is also said that it is a naʿt (adjective) of (سبع). Al-Farrāʾ allowed, outside the Qur'an, (طباق) in the genitive as a naʿt of (سموات).

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying (نورا) and (سراجا): two objects of (جعل), because it means "made into" (صيّر), so it takes two objects. Its like is (بساطا).

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying (من الأرض نباتا): (نبات) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) of a verb indicated by (أنبتكم), i.e. "so you grew a growing". It is also said that it is the maṣdar of (أنبتكم) with the augment dropped.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying (وولده): whoever reads it with ḍamma on the wāw makes it the plural of (ولد), like (وثن) and (وثن) [Translator's note: i.e. waṯan, pl. wuṯn]. It is also said that it is a dialectal form of the singular: one says (ولد) and (ولد) [i.e. walad and wuld], on the pattern of (بخل) and (بخل) [bakhal and bukhl].

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying (ولا يغوث ويعوق): both are accusative by conjunction with (ود). These are names of idols. (يغوث) and (يعوق) are diptotes because they are on the pattern of (يقوم) and (يقول) [Translator's note: the printed text has «بقوم»] and they are definite. Al-Aʿmash read them as fully declinable, which is far-fetched, as if he made them indefinite; and this has no sense, since not every idol is named Yaghūth and Yaʿūq; they are only the names of two known, specific idols, so there is no reason to make them indefinite.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (مما خطيئاتهم): (ما) is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, and (خطيئاتهم) is genitive governed by (من).

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying (من الكافرين ديارا): it is on the pattern fayʿāl from (دار يدور), i.e. "do not leave on the earth anyone of them who moves about". Its origin is (ديوار); then the wāw was assimilated into the yāʾ, like (ميت), whose origin is (ميوت), and then the second was assimilated into the first. It may also be that they replaced the wāw with a yāʾ and then assimilated the first yāʾ into the second. It is not permissible for (ديار) to be on the pattern faʿʿāl, because it would then have to be (دوار), and the word is not so.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿إنا﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿نا﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿أرسلنا﴾: a past verb; ﴿نا﴾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil (agent); and the clause أرسلنا is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿نوحًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إلى قومه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أرسلنا﴾.
﴿أن﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), construed together with what it governs as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ); the (implied) preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿أرسلنا﴾, the meaning being: "We sent him by saying to him: Warn." Or it is explicative (mufassira), because "sending" contains the meaning of "saying".
﴿أنذر﴾: an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿قومك﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿من قبل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أنذر﴾.
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle.
﴿يأتيهم﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يأتيهم﴾ is genitive (majrūr) by annexation.
﴿عذاب﴾: fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿أليم﴾: a naʿt (adjective), nominative.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿قال﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿يا﴾: a vocative particle.
﴿قوم﴾: the one addressed (munādā), in construct (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the first person; and the yāʾ of the first person is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إني﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نذير﴾.
﴿نذير﴾: the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿مبين﴾: a naʿt (adjective), nominative.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿أن﴾: ﴿أن﴾ is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), construed with what follows it as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), i.e.: "that you worship" (بأن اعبدوا). The preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿نذير﴾. And the clause ﴿اعبدوا الله﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the maṣdar-forming ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position. Or ﴿أن﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the clause after it is explicative with no grammatical position.
﴿اعبدوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿واتقوه﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to اعبدوا, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وأطيعون﴾: likewise conjoined, and the omitted yāʾ of the first person is mafʿūl bihi; the yāʾ of the first person was omitted for lightness, to match the verse-endings (fawāṣil).

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿يغفر﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the command; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir).
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يغفر﴾.
﴿من ذنوبكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun in the place of the accusative as the object of يغفر, because من is partitive, i.e.: "some of your sins"; and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿ويؤخركم﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يغفر; its fāʿil is latent, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿إلى أجل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يؤخركم﴾.
﴿مسمى﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿أجل﴾, genitive (majrūr) by an implied (muqaddar) kasra on the alif because pronouncing it is impossible.
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿أجل﴾: the ism (noun) of inna, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb for future time, putting its condition clause in the genitive, attached to its response.
﴿جاء﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent; and the clause جاء is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being put in annexation to it.
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿يؤخر﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is not named (passive); and the clause لا يؤخر has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
﴿لو﴾: conditional.
﴿كنتم﴾: kāna is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its ism.
﴿تعلمون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; and the clause تعلمون is the khabar (predicate) of kāna. The apodosis of لو is omitted, just as the object of تعلمون is omitted, i.e.: "if you knew that, you would believe".

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿قال﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir).
﴿ربّ﴾: the one addressed (munādā), in construct (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb) by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the omitted yāʾ of the first person; the yāʾ of the first person is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the vocative particle is omitted.
﴿إني﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿دعوت﴾: a past verb, and the tāʾ is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; and the clause دعوت is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿قومي﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿ليلا﴾: an adverb, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿دعوت﴾.
﴿ونهارًا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿ليلا﴾; and the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿فلم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿يزدهم﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿دعائي﴾: fāʿil (agent).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿فرارًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi; and the exception is "emptied" (mufarragh, i.e. with no stated excepted-from).

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿وإني﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿كلما﴾: ﴿كلَّ﴾ is a substitute for an adverb of time (nāʾib ẓarf zamān), attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعلوا﴾, containing the meaning of condition; and ﴿ما﴾ is temporal maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya zamāniyya). The clause ﴿دعوتهم﴾ has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative ﴿ما﴾; and ﴿ما﴾ with what it governs is construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is genitive (majrūr) by annexation, its implied form being: "every calling", which is on the omission of a muḍāf, i.e.: "every time of calling". Or ﴿ما﴾ is an indefinite noun qualified by what follows (nakira mawṣūfa), meaning ﴿وقت﴾ ("time"), the referential pronoun being omitted, its implied form being: "every time I called them in it so that You might forgive them"; in that case the clause ﴿دعوتهم﴾ is in the position of the genitive as an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿ما﴾.
﴿دعوتهم﴾: a past verb; the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent), the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿لتغفر﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl), and تغفر is an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām; the implied ﴿أن﴾ and the imperfect verb after it are construed as a maṣdar that is genitive by the causal lām; and the causal lām with its genitive noun are attached to ﴿دعوتهم﴾.
﴿لهم﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تغفر﴾.
﴿جعلوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; and the clause جعلوا has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, namely كلما.
﴿أصابعهم﴾: the first object of جعلوا; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿في آذانهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿جعلوا﴾ in the sense of "they placed".
﴿واستغشوا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جعلوا.
﴿ثيابهم﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi, and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿وأصروا واستكبروا﴾: likewise two conjoined (verbs).
﴿استكبارا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). And the condition clause with its apodosis is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿ثم﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay (tarākhī).
﴿إني﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿دعوتهم﴾: a past verb; the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause دعوتهم is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿جهارًا﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a type of the maṣdar or its attribute; it may also be a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e.: "openly", or "possessing openness".

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿ثم﴾: ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay (tarākhī).
﴿إني﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the yāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿أعلنت﴾: a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أعلنت﴾. And the clause أعلنت is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿وأسررت﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to أعلنت.
﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أسررت﴾.
﴿إسرارًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿فقلت﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; قلت is a past verb, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿استغفروا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿ربكم﴾: the word رب is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إنه﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its ism (noun).
﴿كان﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, its ism latent (mustatir).
﴿غفارا﴾: the khabar (predicate) of kāna, accusative (manṣūb); the clause كان is the khabar of inna; the clause استغفروا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and the clause إنه كان غفارًا has no grammatical position, because it gives the reason for seeking forgiveness.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿يرسل﴾: يرسل is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the command; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), referring to Allah the Exalted.
﴿السماء﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿عليكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يرسل﴾.
﴿مدرارا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from السماء.

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿ويمددكم﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يرسل: يمدد is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), conjoined to يرسل; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿بأموال﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يمددكم﴾.
﴿وبنين﴾: conjoined to أموال.
﴿ويجعل﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to ﴿ويمددكم﴾.
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿جنات﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ويجعل لكم أنهارًا﴾: conjoined to the preceding clause.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of ما.
﴿لا﴾: negating.
﴿ترجون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause لا ترجون is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the kāf in لكم.
﴿لله﴾: the lām is a preposition and the Name of Majesty is a genitive noun; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted ḥāl, because the lām is for clarification (tabyīn); had it come later, it would have been an attribute (ṣifa) of ﴿الوقار﴾. [Translator's note: so in the source, with the article; the word in the ayah is ﴿وقارا﴾.]
﴿وقارا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿ترجون﴾.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿وقد﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq).
﴿خلقكم﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of ترجون.
﴿أطوارًا﴾: a ḥāl interpreted as a derived word (muʾawwala bi-l-mushtaqq), i.e.: "passing from one state to another".

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (istifhām inkārī), and لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿تروا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the "seeing" is cognitive (ʿilmiyya), i.e.: "have you not taken heed and reflected?"
﴿كيف﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the governing word for it being خلق.
﴿خلق﴾: a past verb.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause stands in place of the two objects of تروا, which is suspended from operating (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.
﴿سبع﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿سماوات﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿طباقًا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿سبع﴾, or accusative by an omitted verb, i.e.: "they were layered in layers" (طبقت طباقًا); it would then be the maṣdar of طابقت, (whose maṣdars are) مطابقة and طباق.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿وجعل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جعل is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir).
﴿القمر﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فيهن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعل﴾.
﴿نورًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi.
﴿وجعل الشمس سراجًا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding clause.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿والله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الله is mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أنبتكم﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause أنبتكم is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ.
﴿من الأرض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنبتكم﴾.
﴿نباتا﴾: standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar).

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction.
﴿يعيدكم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يعيدكم﴾.
﴿ويخرجكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and يخرجكم is an imperfect verb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿يعيدكم﴾, nominative; its fāʿil is latent, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi.
