﴿إخراجا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿والله﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and الله is mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿جعل﴾: جعل is a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); and the clause جعل is the khabar (predicate).
﴿لكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعل﴾.
﴿الأرض﴾: first mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿بساطًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿لتسلكوا﴾: the lām is the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl), and تسلكوا is an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause; the implied ﴿أن﴾ and the imperfect verb after it are construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is genitive by the lām of cause; and the lām of cause with its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿جعل﴾.
﴿منها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿سبلا﴾.
﴿سبلا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿فجاجا﴾: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿قال﴾: a past verb.
﴿نوح﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿رب﴾: the one addressed (munādā), accusative (manṣūb), in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the first person; and the omitted yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿إنهم﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and ﴿هم﴾ is its ism (noun).
﴿عصوني﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied ḍamma on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the wāw is the fāʿil; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya); and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause عصوني is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the (whole) clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
﴿واتبعوا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to عصوني.
﴿من﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi.
﴿لم﴾: a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿يزده﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ماله﴾: fāʿil, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿وولده﴾: conjoined to ماله.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿خسارًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi of ﴿يزده﴾.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿ومكروا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; مكروا is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿مكرا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿كبارا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿مكرا﴾.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿وقالوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; قالوا is a past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿لا﴾: prohibitive (nāhiya).
﴿تذرن﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil; and the doubled nūn is the heavy nūn of emphasis (nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīla).
﴿آلهتكم﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ولا تذرن﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first لا تذرن.
﴿ودًّا﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is connective (ṣila).
﴿سواعا﴾: conjoined to ﴿ودًّا﴾, accusative by the fatḥa.
﴿ولا يغوث﴾: likewise conjoined to ﴿ودا﴾.
﴿ويعوق﴾: likewise conjoined to ﴿ودا﴾; and the two words ﴿يغوث ويعوق﴾ are diptotes (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) because of being proper names and having the pattern of a verb, if they are Arabic, and because of being proper names and foreign, if they are non-Arabic.
﴿ونسرا﴾: likewise conjoined to ﴿ودا﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿وقد﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and قد is a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq); the clause قد أضلوا is the object of an omitted saying conjoined to the preceding قال, i.e.: "he said: They have disobeyed me, and he said: They have led astray".
﴿أضلوا﴾: a verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿كثيرًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw conjoins to the omitted saying, and لا is the lā of request, for supplication (duʿāʾ).
﴿تزد﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾.
﴿الظالمين﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿ضلالا﴾: mafʿūl bihi.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿مما﴾: من is a preposition, and ما is connective (ṣila).
﴿خطيئاتهم﴾: genitive (majrūr) by the causal من; the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أغرقوا﴾.
﴿أغرقوا﴾: a past verb whose agent is not named (passive), and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
﴿فأدخلوا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿أغرقوا﴾.
﴿نارا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), by extension of usage (ʿalā al-saʿa).
﴿فلم﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to the past) and jussive.
﴿يجدوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn; and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿لهم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second object.
﴿من دون﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أنصارا﴾: the first object of ﴿يجدوا﴾.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿وقال﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and قال is a past verb.
﴿نوح﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿رب﴾: the one addressed (munādā), accusative (manṣūb), in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the first person; and the omitted yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿لا﴾: the lā of request, for supplication (duʿāʾ).
﴿تذر﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾.
﴿على الأرض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تذر﴾.
﴿من الكافرين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) from ﴿ديارا﴾.
﴿ديارا﴾: the object of تذر.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿إنك﴾: inna is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the kāf is its ism (noun); and the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya).
﴿إن﴾: conditional.
﴿تذرهم﴾: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), jussive (majzūm); its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿يضلوا﴾: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn; and the wāw is the fāʿil; and the protasis with its apodosis is the khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿عبادك﴾: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negating.
﴿يلدوا﴾: an imperfect verb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿يضلوا﴾, jussive; and the wāw is the fāʿil.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿فاجرا﴾: the object of يضلوا. [Translator's note: so in the source; ﴿فاجرا﴾ is the object of ﴿يلدوا﴾, the verb it follows.]
﴿كفارا﴾: a naʿt (adjective).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿رب﴾: the one addressed (munādā), accusative (manṣūb), in construct with the omitted yāʾ of the first person; and the omitted yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿اغفر﴾: a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ), and the fāʿil (agent) is "you" (أنت).
﴿لي﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿اغفر﴾.
﴿ولوالدي﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لوالدي is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿لي﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ; and the yāʾ of the first person is muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿ولمن﴾: likewise conjoined.
﴿دخل﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir).
﴿بيتي﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative by an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ of the first person; and the yāʾ of the first person is muḍāf ilayhi; and the clause ﴿دخل بيتي﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿مؤمنا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative.
﴿وللمؤمنين﴾: likewise conjoined.
﴿والمؤمنات﴾: likewise conjoined.
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is the lā of request, for supplication.
﴿تزد﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾.
﴿الظالمين﴾: first mafʿūl bihi, accusative by the yāʾ.
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿تبارا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: إِنَّا: the origin is "innanā"; the nūn was dropped for lightness. أَرْسَلْنا: the lām was made quiescent in origin because of the succession of vowels and because it is indeclinable (mabnī). نُوحاً: a foreign noun, declined because it has three letters. إِلى قَوْمِهِ: a collective noun; and it has been said: "qawm" is the plural of "qāʾim", like "tājir" and "tajr". أَنْ أَنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ: «أن» has the sense of explication; you say: "i.e., warn your people". It may also be in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "that he should warn your people" [Translator's note: so in the text, «بأن أنذر قومك»; i.e. "with [the message]: warn your people"]. مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذابٌ أَلِيمٌ: you put "qabl" in the genitive by "min" and inflected it because it is in construct with «أن».

nahhas-irab:2-3.t: أَنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ: "an" here too may be in the sense of «أي» (that is), and it may be in the sense of "a warner [telling you] to worship Allah", its ṣila (relative clause) being "uʿbudū". وَاتَّقُوهُ وَأَطِيعُونِ: conjoined to it.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: يَغْفِرْ لَكُمْ مِنْ ذُنُوبِكُمْ: jussive because it is the answer to the command. وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى: conjoined to it. إِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ إِذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ: the imperfect verb is not made jussive by "law" because it differs from the conditional particles in that it does not turn the past into the future.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t:
وَإِنِّي كُلَّما دَعَوْتُهُمْ: accusative as an adverb (ẓarf); and «ما» is joined to «كل» when it is in the sense of "idhā" (when). The answer is جَعَلُوا أَصابِعَهُمْ فِي آذانِهِمْ: the singular is "iṣbaʿ", feminine; one also says "uṣbuʿ".
وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ وَأَصَرُّوا: conjoined to it. Al-Farrāʾ said:
أَصَرُّوا: they persisted silently in disbelief.
وَاسْتَكْبَرُوا اسْتِكْباراً: a maṣdar (verbal noun) carrying the sense of emphasis, and likewise ثُمَّ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُهُمْ جِهاراً; the implied form may also be "possessing openness".

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: إِسْراراً: also a maṣdar (verbal noun) carrying the sense of emphasis.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكُمْ: that is, ask Him for forgiveness. إِنَّهُ كانَ غَفَّاراً: that is, covering over the punishments of sins for whoever repents.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ: the answer to the command. مِدْراراً: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from "al-samāʾ". The pattern mifʿāl is used for the feminine without hāʾ because it runs parallel to the verb; one says "imraʾatun midhkārun" (a woman who bears males) and "miʾnāthun" (who bears females) without hāʾ.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: It is reported that this was said to them because they had an intense love of wealth.

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
Most of the exegetes hold that "al-aṭwār" (stages) means His creating you a drop of fluid, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh. And it has been said:
the diversity of appearances, because you see the creatures and distinguish between them in forms and speech; there must be a difference even if they resemble one another. That indicates a Disposer and Maker.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
طِباقاً: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it may also be a naʿt (adjective) of "sabʿ". Al-Farrāʾ permitted
the genitive outside the Qur'an.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
وَجَعَلَ الْقَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُوراً: Abū Jaʿfar said: the most eminent thing reported about it is the saying of ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr:
the face of the moon is towards the heavens, so it is truly in them. وَجَعَلَ الشَّمْسَ سِراجاً: two objects ...

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) of "anbata" is "inbāt"; however, the implied form is "fa-nabatum nabātan" (and you grew a growing). It has been said: this is because Adam ﷺ was created from clay; and it has been said: the drop of fluid is created from dust.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيها: by burial. وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْراجاً: to the resurrection.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: [Bisāṭan] may also be [spelled] with a ṣād, because a ṭāʾ follows it.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa reported from Ibn ʿAbbās: سُبُلًا فِجاجاً: he said: various roads.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t:
The Kufans and Abū ʿAmr read وَوَلَدُهُ [i.e. "wa-wulduhu"] [Translator's note: the vowelled text reproduces the standard reading, not the variant described];
"wa-wāliduhu" [Translator's note: so in the text, «والده»; perhaps «وُلْده/أُلده» "uldahu", with hamza for wāw, was intended, as the comparison with «أقّتت» suggests] is also permissible, like «أقّتت». Shibl reported from Mujāhid, who said: "wulduhu" is his wife and family. Khārija reported from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, who said: "wulduhu" is his clan and people. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for the lexicographers, apart from this report from Abū ʿAmr, they say: "walad" and "wuld" are like "bakhal" and "bukhl", and "falak" and "fulk"; and in their view "wuld" may be the plural of "walad", [like] "wathan" and "wuthn".

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
And «كُبَّاراً» [Translator's note: the variant reading referred to is not shown; presumably "kubāran", without doubling]:
it is a reading with the same meaning.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t:
وَقالُوا لا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَلا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلا سُواعاً: this [i.e. "wuddan", with ḍamma] is the reading of the people of Medina; the Kufans and Abū ʿAmr read وَدًّا with fatḥa on the wāw, which is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He argued from their saying "ʿAbd Wadd" and that the idol's name was "Wadd". [Translator's note: the vowelled text shows «وَدًّا» in both places; the Medinan reading described is "wuddan".] Abū Jaʿfar said: this is among the anomalous arguments; what is commonly known is the reverse of what he said: one says only "ʿAbd Wudd" [Translator's note: so in the text, the vowelling being implied]. If it is a matter of common usage, then it is this; and if it is a matter of what is most fitting, then the most fitting is that it should be named "Wudd", derived from "al-widād", which is ease and softness. From it comes "wadidtu al-rajula", I loved the man, and "wadadtuhu" when I treated him kindly; and "wadidtu anna dhālika al-shayʾa lī", i.e. I wished with ease [that the thing were mine]; and their naming the idol "Wudd" is from this. وَلا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْراً: "Yaghūth" and "Yaʿūq" are not declined (lam yanṣarif) because they resemble the imperfect verb. Al-Aʿmash read «ولا يغوث ويعوق» declined [i.e. "yaghūthan wa-yaʿūqan"]. In the text (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh, according to what is reported: وَلا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلا سُواعاً وَلا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْراً [with tanwīn on "Yaghūth" and "Yaʿūq"] [Translator's note: the vowelled text shows the standard reading]. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, a solecism (laḥn), and it also contradicts the great body of the written text (al-sawād al-aʿẓam). Al-Farrāʾ claimed
that declining it is permissible because of its frequency, or as though it were indefinite. This does not hold, because it is not the case that when a thing is frequent, what is diptote in it becomes declined; besides, his saying
"because of its frequency" has no meaning for the name of an idol, and it has no meaning for something specific like this to be indefinite. Al-Kisāʾī went further than this and said: the Arabs decline every diptote except "afʿalu minka" (more … than you). Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this is wrong, because they have declined "khayran minka" and "sharran minka", with "minka" accompanying them.

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا كَثِيراً: outside the Qur'an, "wa-qad aḍlalna" and "wa-qad aḍallat" would be permissible. وَلا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلالًا: it has been said: the meaning is "do not grant them success"; and it has been said: except straying from the reward and the way to Paradise.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t:
«ما» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis; according to the Basrans nothing else is permissible. The Kufans say:
a connective (ṣila), and then in some places they return to the truth, and this is one of them. Al-Farrāʾ claimed ]
that «ما» here adds meaning, because the meaning is "because of their sins they were drowned", and he argued that «ما» indicates the conditional (mujāzāh), and mentioned "ḥaythumā takun akun" (wherever you are, I shall be), and mentioned "kayfa" and "ayna" — this is in his book «Maʿānī al-Qurʾān». His position in this would be good were it not for the confusion in it: he mentioned "ḥaythumā", with which the conditional is formed only when «ما» accompanies it; and he mentioned «كيف», with which the conditional is not formed at all; and he mentioned «أين», with which the conditional is formed both with «ما» and without «ما». So he combined three different things.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: That is, anyone; it is from "dāra yadūru", i.e. anyone who moves about. And it has been said: "dayyār" is the occupant of a dwelling (dār).

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا عِبادَكَ وَلا يَلِدُوا إِلاَّ فاجِراً كَفَّاراً (27). إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ: a condition. يُضِلُّوا عِبادَكَ: the apodosis (mujāzāh). وَلا يَلِدُوا إِلَّا فاجِراً كَفَّاراً: conjoined to it.

safi-cedvel:1-1.t:
* I'rab:
(إلى قومه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أرسلنا), (أن) particle of explication [Note: Or a maṣdar particle ... and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (أرسلنا) in the first verse, and attached to نذير in the second and third verses.], (من قبل) attached to (أنذر), (أن) maṣdar and subjunctive particle.
The clause «إنّا أرسلنا ...» has no grammatical position: initial (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «أرسلنا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «أنذر ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «يأتيهم عذاب ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتيهم ...) is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.

safi-cedvel:2-4.t:
* I'rab:
(قوم) the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf, accusative; the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the (ياء) that was dropped for lightness, which is muḍāf ilayhi; (لكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) (نذير); (أن) particle of explication [Note: Or a maṣdar particle ... and the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, attached to (أرسلنا) in the first verse, and attached to نذير in the second and third verses.], (الواو) conjunction in both places; and (النون) in (أطيعون) is the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) before the (ياء) of the first person, which has been dropped to suit the verse-ending, and which is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يغفر) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), answer of the imperative in the preceding verbs; (لكم) attached to (يغفر), (من ذنوبكم) attached to (يغفر), and (من) is partitive; (الواو) conjunction; (يؤخّركم) imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (يغفر); (إلى أجل) attached to (يؤخّركم), (إذا) adverb for future time including the meaning of condition, in the position of an accusative, attached to the apodosis لا يؤخّر [Note: Or an adverb stripped of the conditional meaning, attached to the khabar of إنّ (لا يؤخّر).], (لو) non-jussivising conditional particle ...
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the vocative and its answer ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «إنّي ... نذير» has no grammatical position: the answer of the vocative.
The clause «اعبدوا ...» has no grammatical position: explicative.
The clause «اتّقوه ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the explicative clause.
The clause «أطيعون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the explicative clause.
The clause «يغفر ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ [Note: I.e. "if you worship Allah ... He will forgive you".].
The clause «يؤخّركم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يغفر.
The clause «إنّ أجل الله» has no grammatical position; it carries the meaning of causation ...
The clause «the condition, its verb and its answer» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of إنّ.
The clause «جاء ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «لا يؤخّر ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivising condition [Note: Or it is the khabar of (إنّ) in the case where (إذا) is stripped of the condition.].
The clause «كنتم تعلمون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive ... The answer of لو is omitted, its implied form being "you would have believed".
The clause «تعلمون» is in the position of an accusative, khabar of كنتم.

* Benefits:
- Is the term postponed when it comes?
In this passage there occurs the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى», then Allah the Exalted said «إِنَّ أَجَلَ اللَّهِ إِذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ لَوْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ». Its meaning is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says:
Believe before death and you will be safe from the punishment, for the term of Allah — which is death — when it comes is not postponed. Al-Zamakhsharī said: If you say: How did He say "and He will postpone you" along with informing that postponing the term is impossible — is this not a contradiction?! I say: He decreed — for example — that the people of Noah, if they believed, He would let them live a thousand years, and if they persisted in their disbelief, He would destroy them at the end of nine hundred years. So it was said to them: Believe and He will postpone you to a named term, i.e. a time that Allah has named and set as a limit at which you end and which you do not exceed, and that is the longer time, the completion of the thousand. Then He informed that when that term comes it is not postponed as this time is postponed, and you will have no device; so hasten during the times of respite and postponement granted to you, and while belief is possible for you.
It has also been said: they feared for themselves being destroyed by their own people because of their believing and responding to Noah, upon him be blessings and peace; so it is as if he, upon him be blessings and peace, assured them of safety from that, and promised them that by their believing they would remain until the term that had been set for them had they not believed, i.e. "by your submitting you will remain safe from your enemy until the term that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has written for you."

safi-cedvel:5-9.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) the one addressed (munādā), muḍāf, accusative; the sign of the accusative is the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the (ياء) of the first person that was dropped for lightness, which is muḍāf ilayhi; (ليلا) adverb of time, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (دعوت), (الفاء) conjunction; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (فرارا) second mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.
The clause «قال ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the vocative ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, a supplication seeking mercy.
The clause «إنّي دعوت ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «دعوت ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «لم يزدهم دعائي ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the object of the saying.
7- (الواو) conjunction; (كلّما) a conditional adverb in the position of an accusative, attached to the apodosis جعلوا [Note: It is permissible for (كلّ) to be an adverb annexed to the interpreted maṣdar formed from (ما) and the verb.], (اللام) causal; (تغفر) imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām; (لهم) attached to (تغفر), (في آذانهم) attached to (جعلوا), i.e. "they put"; (الواو) conjunction in the three places; (استكبارا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative.
The clause «إنّي كلّما ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause إنّي دعوت ...
The clause «the condition, its verb and its answer ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of إنّ.
The clause «دعوتهم ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi. The clause «تغفر ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تغفر) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (دعوتهم).
The clause «جعلوا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussivising condition.
The clause «استغشوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis.
The clause «أصرّوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis.
The clause «استكبروا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the apodosis.
8-9 (ثمّ) conjunction; (جهارا) mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun) [Note: Because it is its kind, i.e. a call of openness, or because it is its adjective, i.e. an open call ... Or it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "openly".], (لهم) attached to (أعلنت), and the second is attached to (أسررت), (إسرارا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative.
The clause «إنّي دعوتهم ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the object of the saying.
The clause «دعوتهم ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of (the third) إنّ.
The clause «إنّي أعلنت ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause إنّي دعوتهم.
The clause «أعلنت ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of (the fourth) إنّ.
The clause «أسررت ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause أعلنت.

* Morphology:
(6) يزدهم: in it there is iʿlāl (phonological change) by deletion because of the meeting of two quiescents, occasioned by the jussive with (لم); its origin is يزيدهم ... its pattern is يفهم [Translator's note: so in the source; the usual measure given is يفلهم].
(7) استغشوا: in it there is iʿlāl by deletion: the lām of the word was deleted because it met, quiescent, with the wāw of the plural, and the letter before the wāw remained with fatḥa to indicate the deleted alif; its pattern is استفعوا — with fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(8) جهارا: a non-analogical (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb جهر, of the class of فتح; its pattern is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ. It is also a samāʿī maṣdar of the quadriliteral جاهر, because its analogical maṣdar is مجاهرة.

* Rhetoric:
Hyperbole (mubālagha): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَاسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ».
I.e. they went to extremes in covering themselves with them, as if they asked their garments to cover them, so as not to see him, out of dislike of looking at him, from the excess of their dislike of the call. In expressing it with the istifʿāl form there is a hyperbole that is not hidden.
Repetition (takrīr): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «ثُمَّ إِنِّي أَعْلَنْتُ لَهُمْ وَأَسْرَرْتُ لَهُمْ إِسْراراً».
He mentioned that he called them by night and by day, then called them openly, then called them in secret and in public. These had to be three different calls for the conjunction to be valid. The reason for that is that the prophet ﷺ [Translator's note: so in the source; the reference here is to Noah, upon him be peace.] did as one who enjoins good and forbids evil does: beginning with the gentlest and rising to the more severe, then the more severe. So he began with sincere advice in secret; when they did not accept, he followed up with openness; and when that had no effect, he thirdly combined secrecy and openness.

* Benefits:
- كلّما:
كلما is accusative as an adverb by agreement, attached to the answer. So in the saying of Allah the Exalted in the verse we are dealing with (وَإِنِّي كُلَّما دَعَوْتُهُمْ لِتَغْفِرَ لَهُمْ جَعَلُوا أَصابِعَهُمْ فِي آذانِهِمْ) it is attached to the verb (جعلوا). Its adverbial sense came to it from the side of (ما), and nothing follows it but the past tense, in both condition and answer, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted (كُلَّما نَضِجَتْ جُلُودُهُمْ بَدَّلْناهُمْ جُلُوداً غَيْرَها لِيَذُوقُوا الْعَذابَ) (كُلَّما أَضاءَ لَهُمْ مَشَوْا فِيهِ) (كُلَّما مَرَّ عَلَيْهِ مَلَأٌ مِنْ قَوْمِهِ سَخِرُوا مِنْهُ).
And if you say: (كلما استدعيتك فإن زرتني فعبدي حر) (Whenever I summon you, then if you visit me, my slave is free), (كلما) is also accusative as an adverb, but its governor is omitted, indicated by (حرّ) mentioned in the answer; it is not the mentioned governor, because that occurs after the fāʾ and إنّ [Translator's note: so in the source; the example has the conditional إن, not إنّ]. The clause occurring after (كلما) is in the position of a genitive by annexation; as for the answer of the condition, it has no grammatical position because it is the answer of a non-jussivising condition.

safi-cedvel:10-14.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction; (يرسل) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), answer of the imperative, given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescents; (السماء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: With the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the rain of the sky ... Or السماء is used as a majāz mursal (metonymic trope), the relation being one of place.], (عليكم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يرسل), (مدرارا) ḥāl (circumstantial) of السماء [Note: It is not made feminine because the pattern مفعال is the same for masculine and feminine.], accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (يمددكم) imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (يرسل), (بأموال) attached to (يمددكم), (يجعل) jussive, conjoined to (يرسل), (لكم) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi; (يجعل لكم أنهارا) like يجعل لكم جنّات ...
The clause «قلت ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause أسررت [Note: In the preceding verse (9).].
The clause «استغفروا ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «إنّه كان ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «كان غفّارا ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «يرسل ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of an implied condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «يمددكم ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يرسل.
The clause «يجعل (the first)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يرسل.
The clause «يجعل (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يرسل.
13-14 (ما) interrogative noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject); (لكم) attached to the khabar of the mubtadaʾ ما; (لا) negative; (لله) attached to a ḥāl of (وقارا), (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (قد) particle of realisation; (أطوارا) ḥāl, accusative, i.e. "passing through changing states" ...
The clause «ما لكم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive, within the scope of the saying.
The clause «لا ترجون ...» is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl.
The clause «خلقكم ...» is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl of the agent of ترجون.

* Morphology:
(13) وقارا: maṣdar (verbal noun) of وقر, of the class of كرم, i.e. "he became dignified"; its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ ... or a noun meaning dignity.
(14) أطوارا: plural of طور, a noun meaning state, form and time (occasion); its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn, and the plural is أفعال.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymic trope (al-majāz al-mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِدْراراً».
The relation of this trope is locality: by السماء He meant rain, because rain comes down from the sky.

safi-cedvel:15-20.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation; (كيف) interrogative noun in the position of an accusative, ḥāl (circumstantial); (طباقا) ḥāl, accusative, of سبع سموات; (الواو) conjunction in both places; (فيهنّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (جعل) [Note: The genitive pronoun refers to the heavens according to the apparent sense, not in reality.].
The clause «لم تروا ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «خلق الله ...» is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of seeing, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative كيف.
The clause «جعل (the first) ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause خلق الله.
The clause «جعل (the second) ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause خلق الله.
17-18 (الواو) resumptive; (من الأرض) attached to (أنبتكم), i.e. "He brought you into being"; (نباتا) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar (verbal noun), since it meets it in derivation; (ثم) conjunction; (فيها) attached to (يعيدكم), (إخراجا) mafʿūl muṭlaq, accusative ...
The clause «الله أنبتكم ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أنبتكم ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (الله).
The clause «يعيدكم ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause أنبتكم.
The clause «يخرجكم ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause يعيدكم.
19-20 (الواو) conjunction; (لكم) attached to (جعل) [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl of (بساطا).], (اللام) causal; (تسلكوا) imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām; (منها) attached to (تسلكوا) by making it include the meaning of تتّخذوا [Note: Or attached to a ḥāl of (سبلا).] ... (فجاجا) naʿt (adjective) of (سبلا) — or a badal (substitute) of it.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تسلكوا) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (جعل) [Note: Or attached to (بساطا), because it has the meaning of مبسوطة (spread out).].
The clause «الله جعل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause الله أنبتكم.
The clause «جعل (the third) ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «تسلكوا ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(19) بساطا: a noun for what is spread on the floor of a room; it came in the verse by way of simile.

* Rhetoric:
The explicit dependent metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya al-tabaʿiyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَباتاً».
I.e. He brought you into being from it. "Causing to grow" was borrowed for "bringing into being", because it is more indicative of origination and coming into existence from the earth, being perceptible to the senses, and its perception has been repeated. And although they did not deny origination, they were made, by their denial of the resurrection, like one who denied it. So in the speech there is an explicit dependent metaphor.

safi-cedvel:21-25.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّ) its i'rab has preceded [Note: In verse (5) of this sūra.], (عصوني) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescents; (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent), (النون) is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and (الياء) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) conjunction in both places; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (خسارا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «قال نوح ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «the vocative and its answer ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying).
The clause «إنّهم عصوني ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the vocative.
The clause «عصوني ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «اتّبعوا ...» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause عصوني.
The clause «لم يزده ماله ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من). The clause «مكروا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause [Note: I.e. "they followed those who plotted a tremendous plot". It may also be conjoined to the clause عصوني, in which case it is in the position of a nominative.].
23- (الواو) conjunction in the six places; (لا) prohibitive, jussivising; (تذرنّ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn; the (الواو), deleted because of the meeting of two quiescents, is the agent, and (النون) is the nūn of emphasis; (لا) like the first; and the third and fourth are redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the prohibition [Note: (يغوث ويعوق) are denied tanwīn (diptotes) because of being proper names and foreign, or because of being proper names and having the pattern of a verb.].
The clause «قالوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause [Note: Or conjoined to the clause عصوني, in the position of a nominative.].
The clause «لا تذرنّ ... (the first)» is in the position of an accusative, object of the saying.
The clause «لا تذرنّ ... (the second)» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause of the object of the saying.
24- (الواو) conjunction in both places; (قد) particle of realisation; (لا) prohibitive, jussivising — of supplication; (إلّا) for restriction; (ضلالا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
The clause «قد أضلّوا ...» is in the position of an accusative, object of an implied saying, i.e. "Noah said" [Note: This implied saying has no grammatical position, being conjoined to His saying: قال نوح ربّ إنّهم عصوني.].
The clause «لا تزد ...» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause قد أضلّوا.
25- (ما) redundant; (من خطيئاتهم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أغرقوا), and (من) is causal; (الواو) in (أغرقوا) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and likewise the wāw in (أدخلوا); (الفاء) conjunction in both places; (من دون) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (أنصارا), (لهم) attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi.
The clause «أغرقوا ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أدخلوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أغرقوا.
The clause «لم يجدوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أدخلوا.

* Morphology:
(22) كبّارا: intensive form from the triliteral كبر; its pattern is فعّال, with ḍamma on the fāʾ and a doubled ʿayn with fatḥa.
(23) ودّا: the name of an idol. It has been said that he was one of the sons of Adam, for whom a statue was made after his death bearing his name. Its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn — or with ḍamma then sukūn according to the reading of Nāfiʿ. (سواعا) the name of one of the idols of the Jāhiliyya; its pattern is فعال with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(يغوث): it is like ودّ ... its pattern is يفعل with ḍamma on the ʿayn; then it underwent iʿlāl (phonological change) by making the wāw quiescent and transferring its vowel to the ghayn.
(يعوق): like يغوث in meaning and morphology.
(نسرا): like ودّ in pattern and meaning.

* Benefits:
- Redundant (ما):
Among the places where (ما) is added is after the genitive-governing particle (i.e. the preposition), as in the saying of Allah the Exalted in the verse we are dealing with (مِمَّا خَطِيئاتِهِمْ), and (فَبِما رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ) and (عَمَّا قَلِيلٍ لَيُصْبِحُنَّ نادِمِينَ). And the poet's saying:
وننصر مولانا ونعلم أنه ... كما الناس مجروم عليه وجارم
(We support our ally, knowing that he, like people, is sometimes wronged and sometimes does wrong.)
It is added after a genitive-governing word that is a noun, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted (أَيَّمَا الْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلا عُدْوانَ عَلَيَّ).
It is added after the jussivising particle, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «إِمَّا يَنْزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ نَزْغٌ فَاسْتَعِذْ بِاللَّهِ» (أيّا ما تدعو), and the saying of al-Aʿshā:
متى ما تناخي عند باب ابن هاشم ... تراحي وتلقى من فواضله ندى
(Whenever you [my she-camel] kneel at the door of Ibn Hāshim, you will rest and meet bounty from his favours.) And Ibn Hāshim is the Messenger Muḥammad ﷺ.
It is added after a conditional particle, whether jussivising, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: (أَيْنَما تَكُونُوا يُدْرِكْكُمُ الْمَوْتُ), or non-jussivising, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted (حَتَّى إِذا ما جاؤُها شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ سَمْعُهُمْ).
It is added between the followed word and its follower, as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: «مَثَلًا ما بَعُوضَةً». And al-Aʿshā added it twice in his saying:
إما ترينا حفاة لا نعال لنا ... إنا كذلك ما نحفى وننتعل
(If you see us barefoot, without sandals — so are we: at times we go barefoot and at times we are shod.)

safi-cedvel:26-28.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, jussivising; (على الأرض) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تذر), (من الكافرين) attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (ديّارا). The clause «قال نوح ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause قال نوح [Note: In verse (21) of this sūra.].
The clause «the vocative and its answer ...» is in the position of an accusative, maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying) [Note: Or the vocative clause is parenthetical, and the clause لا تذر is the object of the saying.].
The clause «لا تذر ...» has no grammatical position: the answer of the vocative.
27- (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative; (يلدوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (يضلّوا), the apodosis; (إلّا) for restriction (ḥaṣr); (فاجرا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative [Note: In the speech there is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope) by consideration of what will be; Noah said that after it had been revealed to him what would become of these people.].
The clause «إنّك إن تذرهم ...» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «إن تذرهم ...» is in the position of a nominative, khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «يضلّوا ...» has no grammatical position: apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a jussivising condition, not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا يلدوا ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يضلّوا.
28- (لي) attached to (اغفر), (الواو) conjunction in the five places; (لوالديّ، لمن) both attached to (اغفر), being conjoined to (لي); (مؤمنا) ḥāl, accusative, of the agent of دخل; (للمؤمنين) attached to (اغفر), conjoined to (لي); (المؤمنات) conjoined to المؤمنين, genitive; (لا تزد الظالمين إلّا تبارا) like لا تزد الظالمين إلّا ضلالا [Note: In verse (24) of this sūra.].
The clause «ربّ ...» has no grammatical position: parenthetical, seeking mercy.
The clause «اغفر ...» has no grammatical position: a resumption within the scope of the saying.
The clause «دخل ...» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «لا تزد الظالمين» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause اغفر.

* Morphology:
(26) ديّارا: a noun meaning "anyone". It has been said to be taken from الدار, i.e. one who dwells in a house; and it has been said to be taken from الدوران, which is movement. In it there is iʿlāl (phonological change) by substitution: its origin is ديوار; the yāʾ and the wāw came together, the first being quiescent, so the wāw was changed to yāʾ and assimilated into the first yāʾ. Its pattern is فيعال.
(27) يلدوا: in it there is iʿlāl by deletion: the fāʾ of the word was deleted from it in the imperfect, for it is a mithāl (first-radical-weak) verb with kasra on the ʿayn in the imperfect; its pattern is يعلوا.
(فاجرا): active participle from the triliteral فجر, of the class of نصر; its pattern is فاعل.
(28) تبارا: the noun from تبر يتبر, of the class of نصر or the class of فرح, meaning "to perish" ... or it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the quadriliteral تبرّ; its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
Metonymic trope (majāz mursal): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَلا يَلِدُوا إِلَّا فاجِراً كَفَّاراً».
The relation of this trope is what it will lead to, because they were not wicked at the time of birth, but in any case only a long time after it. I.e. they will beget only those who will be wicked and disbelieve; so He described them by what they will become.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {أَنْ أَنذِرْ}: It may be the explicative «أَنْ» (mufassira), or the maṣdar-forming one (maṣdariyya), that is: "We sent him with the warning." al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: We sent him by saying to him: «أَنْذِرْ» ("warn"), that is: We sent him with the command to warn." End of quotation. What he has implied is very good, and it is an answer to a question I raised earlier on this topic: namely that their statement "the maṣdar-forming «أَنْ» may be joined to the imperative" is problematic, because from it and what follows it a maṣdar is formed, and then the indication of the command is lost. Do you not see that if you imply, in «كَتَبْتُ إليه بأَنْ قُمْ», "I wrote to him standing", the indication of the command is lost at the very point where the command is stated explicitly? So it should be implied as al-Zamakhsharī said, that is: "I wrote to him by saying to him: «قُمْ»", that is, "I wrote to him with the command to stand."

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {أَنِ اعبدوا}: It is either explicative (tafsīriyya) of «نذير», or maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and the discussion of it is as given above for its sister.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمْ}: There are several views about this «مِنْ». First: that it is partitive (tabʿīḍiyya). Second: that it marks the beginning of the range (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya). Third: that it is for clarifying the genus, which is rejected because nothing precedes it for it to clarify. Fourth: that it is redundant (zāʾida). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "This is a Kufan view." I say: that is not their view, because they require only that its genitive noun be indefinite and require nothing else; and al-Akhfash requires nothing, so its redundancy here goes along with his view, not theirs.
His saying: {وَيُؤَخِّرْكُمْ إلى أَجَلٍ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how does He say «ويُؤَخِّرْكم» when He informs that postponement of it is impossible? I say: Allah decreed that if the people of Noah believed, He would give them a life of a thousand years, and if they remained in their disbelief, He would destroy them at the head of nine hundred. So it was said to them: if you believe you will be given respite until the longer term; then He told them that when that furthest term comes it is not postponed." End of quotation. Those who speak of two terms have clung to this verse; the answer to that was given earlier. His saying: {لَوْ كُنتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ}: its apodosis is omitted, that is: "you would have hastened to what He commanded you."

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {لِتَغْفِرَ}: It may be causal (lil-taʿlīl), the thing they were called to being omitted, that is: "I called them to believe in You for the sake of Your forgiving them"; or it may be the lām of transitivity (lām al-taʿdiya), in which case the cause is expressed by the effect, which is their being made so. The original is: "I called them to repentance, which is a cause of forgiveness." «جعلوا» is the governing word in «كلما», and it is the khabar (predicate) of «إنِّي».
His saying: {لَيْلاً وَنَهَاراً}: two adverbials of «دَعَوْت». What is meant is to report the continuity of the calling and that he did not slacken in it. «إلاَّ فِراراً» is a second object, and it is a "voided" exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh).

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {جِهَاراً}: It may be a maṣdar in sense, since calling may be done openly or otherwise, so it falls under the category of «قَعَدَ القُرْفُصاءَ» ("he sat squatting"); or what is meant by «دَعَوْتُهم» is «جاهَرْتُهم» ("I addressed them openly"); or it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "an open calling"; or it may be a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: "openly" or "possessing openness", or the maṣdar itself is made the ḥāl for emphasis. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: He mentioned that he called them night and day, then called them openly, then called them in secret and in public; so these must be three different callings for the conjunction to be sound? I say: he, peace be upon him, acted as one does who enjoins the right and forbids the wrong, beginning with the easier and then advancing to the harsher and harsher. So he began the counsel in secret; when they did not accept, he repeated with open address; when they did not accept, he made a third with a combination of secrecy and publicity. The meaning of «ثم» is to indicate the distance between the states, because open address is harsher than secrecy, and combining the two is harsher than either alone." The Shaykh said: "It has been repeated much by him that «ثُمَّ» expresses remoteness (istibʿād), and we do not know this from anyone else." I say: this statement, after you have heard al-Zamakhsharī's words, is an unfair attack on him.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {مِّدْرَاراً}: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السماء». It is not made feminine because the form مِفْعال is not made feminine. One says: «امرأةٌ مئِنْاثٌ» ("a woman who bears many daughters") and «مِذْكار» ("who bears many sons"), and it takes the tāʾ only rarely, and then masculine and feminine are alike in it, so you say: «رجلٌ مِجْذامَةٌ ومِطْرابَةٌ» and «امرأة مِجْذامَةٌ ومِطْرابَةٌ». Or it may be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: "a copious sending". The discussion of it was given in al-Anʿām.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {وَقَاراً}: It may be a direct object (mafʿūl bihi), with several senses. Among them: "What is the matter with you that you do not expect reverence (تَوْقيراً) for Him, that is, exaltation?" al-Zamakhsharī said: "The meaning is: What is the matter with you that you are not in a state in which you hope for Allah's exalting you in the abode of reward? And «لله» is a clarification of the one revered (al-muwaqqar); had it come later, it would have been a ṣila (connected complement)." End of quotation. That is: had «لله» come after «وَقارا», it would have been attached to it, so the reverence would be from them to Allah the Exalted, which is the opposite of the meaning he intended. Among them also: "You do not fear forbearance from Allah and His leaving off hastening the punishment, so that you would believe." Among them: "You do not fear greatness from Allah." On the first, the hope (rajāʾ) is in its proper sense; it has already been mentioned that its use in the sense of fear is figurative or shared. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «تَرْجُون», that is: "revering Allah the Exalted," that is, exalting Him; then «للَّهِ» is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl from «وَقارا», or the lām is redundant in the direct object, and two things make this fair here: that the governing word is derived (a secondary form), and that the governed word is put first. «لا تَرْجُون» is a ḥāl, and a parallel was given earlier in al-Māʾida.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ}: a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya) from the agent of «تَرْجُون». الأَطْوار means the different states. The poet said:
4340 - فإنْ أفاقَ قد طارَتْ عَمَايَتُه ... والمَرْءُ يُخْلَقُ طَوْراً بعد أطوارِ
(If he recovers, his blindness has flown off; and man is created stage after stage.) It is accusative as ḥāl, that is: "passing from state to state," or "differing, between evildoer and doer of good, righteous and corrupt."

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {طِبَاقاً}: The discussion of it was given in Sūrat al-Mulk. Makkī said: "al-Farrāʾ permitted, outside the Qur'an, the genitive of «طباق» as an adjective of «سماوات»," meaning that it may be an adjective of the number at one time and of the counted noun at another.

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {فِيهِنَّ}: that is, in the heavens, though the moon is in only one heaven of them. It was said: it is in the lowest heaven. This is allowed because there is contiguity between the heavens, so it is sound. One says "Zayd is in the city" when he is only in one corner of its corners.
His saying: {وَجَعَلَ الشمس سِرَاجاً}: The implied form may be: "and He placed the sun in them," as above. As for the sun, it was said: in the fourth heaven; it was said: in the fifth; it was said: in winter in the fourth and in summer in the seventh. Allah knows best which of these is correct.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {نَبَاتاً}: It is either a maṣdar (verbal noun) of «أَنْبَتَ» with the augment letters dropped, called ism maṣdar, or it is governed by an implied «نَبَتُّمْ», that is: "so you grew a growth," so that it is accusative by the implied intransitive form. al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or it is accusative by «أَنْبَتكم», because it includes the meaning of «نَبَتُّمْ»." The Shaykh said: "I cannot make sense of this second view." I say: this view is the one I gave earlier, namely that it is accusative by «أَنْبَتكم» with the augment letters dropped. The meaning of his saying "because it includes the meaning of «نَبَتُّمْ»" is that it contains it; the most that is in it is that its augments were dropped. The "causing to grow" here is an eloquent metaphor.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {سُبُلاً فِجَاجاً}: In al-Anbiyāʾ «الفِجاجُ» was put first, to harmonise the verse endings here. Something like this has already been discussed.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {وَوَلَدُهُ}: The disagreement of the readers about «وَلَدِه» has been given, and it was mentioned that they are two dialectal forms, like بُخْل and بَخَل. Abū Ḥātim said: it is possible that the form with ḍamma is the plural of the form with fatḥa, like خَشَب and خُشْب. He recited for Ḥassān, may Allah be pleased with him:
4341 - يا بِكرَ آمنةَ المباركَ وِلْدُها ... مِنْ وُلْدِ مُحْصَنَةٍ بسَعْدٍ الأَسْعُدِ
(O firstborn of Āmina, whose children are blessed, of the children of a chaste woman, with the luckiest of fortunes.)

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {وَمَكَرُواْ}: It is conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) of «مَنْ». The pronoun is plural only by being carried over to the sense, after being carried over to the form of the word in {لَّمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُ وَوَلَدُهُ}. It may also be a fresh sentence, informing about the unbelievers.
His saying: {كُبَّاراً}: The majority read it with ḍamma on the kāf and shadda on the bāʾ, a form of intensification stronger than «كُبار» with ḍamma and light bāʾ. ʿĪsā said: it is a Yemeni dialect, and he recited:
4342 - والمرءُ يُلْحِقُه بفِتيان النَّدى ... خُلُقُ الكريمِ وليس بالوُضَّاء
(A man is brought into the company of the youths of generosity by the character of the noble, not by being handsome.) And the words of another:
4343 - بَيْضاءُ تصطادُ القلوبَ وتَسْتَبي ... بالحسنِ قلبَ المسلمِ القُرَّاء
(A fair one who hunts hearts and captivates with beauty the heart of the Muslim, the reciter.) One says: «رجلٌ طُوَّالٌ وحُمَّالٌ وحُسَّانٌ». ʿĪsā, Abū al-Sammāl and Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with ḍamma and a light bāʾ, which is also a form of intensification but less than the first. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Ibn Muḥayṣin also read it with kasra on the kāf and a light bāʾ. Abū Bakr said: it is the plural of «كبير», as though he made «مَكْراً» stand in place of «ذنوب» or «أفاعيل», meaning that is why he described it with a plural.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ تَذَرُنَّ وَدّاً وَلاَ سُوَاعاً}: It may be an instance of conjoining the particular to the general (ʿaṭf al-khāṣṣ ʿalā al-ʿāmm) if it is said that these names are of idols, and it may not be so if it is said that they are names of righteous men, as mentioned in the exegesis. Nāfiʿ read «وُدّاً» with ḍamma on the wāw, and the rest with fatḥa. The words of the poet were recited with both forms:
4344 - حَيَّاكَ وَدٌّ فإنَّا لا يَحِلُّ لنا ... لَهْوُ النساءِ وإنَّ الدين قد عزما
(May Wadd greet you; for we are not permitted the amusement of women, and religion has become resolute.) And the words of another:
4345 - فحيَّاكِ وَدٌّ مِنْ هُداكِ لفِتْيَةٍ ... وخُوْصٍ بأعلى ذي فُضالةَ مُنْجِدِ
(May Wadd greet you, from your guidance, for young men and hollow-eyed camels on the heights of Dhū Fuḍāla, going to the highlands.)
His saying: {وَلاَ يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ}: The majority read both without tanwīn. If they are Arabic, the prohibition of the ṣarf (the diptote status) is because of being proper names and the verb pattern; if they are non-Arabic, it is because of being proper names and foreignness. al-Aʿmash read «ولا يَغُوْثاً ويَعُوْقاً», declined with tanwīn. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "That is a slip, because definiteness is inherent and the verb pattern is present." End of quotation.
It is not a slip, for two reasons. One: that he made them fully declinable for harmony, since before them there are two declinable names and after them a declinable name, just as «سلاسل» was made declinable. The other: that it follows the dialect of those who make the diptote declinable in every case, a dialect related by al-Kisāʾī.
Abū al-Faḍl transmitted the declension of both from al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī, then said: "He made them of the pattern فَعُول, so he declined them; as for the majority, they are two adjectives from الغَوْث and العَوْق." I say: this is problematic speech. As for his saying «فَعُولاً», it is not correct, since the roots «يغث» and «يعق» are non-existent. As for his saying "two adjectives from الغَوْث and العَوْق," there is no «يَفْعُل» among adjectives or nouns, and the correct view is what I gave earlier. al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is a problematic reading, because whether they are Arabic or non-Arabic, they are diptotes; perhaps he intended the pairing (izdiwāj) and so declined them, finding their sisters declinable: وَدّاً, سُوعاً and نَسْراً." The Shaykh said: "It is as though he was not aware that declining what is a diptote is a dialect."

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying: {وَقَدْ أَضَلُّواْ}: that is, the leaders, or the idols; and He gathered them in the plural of rational beings, treating them as rational beings are treated.
His saying: {وَلاَ تَزِدِ}: It is conjoined to His saying: {رَّبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي} [Nūḥ: 21], by way of reporting Noah's speech after «قال» and after the wāw that stands in its place, that is: "He said: 'they disobeyed me,' and said: 'do not increase,'" that is, he said these two sayings, so both are in the position of the accusative. This was said by al-Zamakhsharī. He said: "As you say: «قال زيدٌ: نوديَ للصلاة وصَلِّ في المسجدِ»," reporting his two sayings with one conjoined to the other. The Shaykh said: "«ولا تَزِدْ» is conjoined to «قد أَضَلُّوا», because they are reported by an implied «قال», and correspondence is not required among conjoined clauses; one may conjoin a statement to a request and the reverse, contrary to those who required it."

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {مِّمَّا خطيائاتهم}: «ما» is redundant between the preposition and its genitive noun, for emphasis. Whoever does not hold it redundant makes it indefinite and makes «خطيئاتِهم» a badal (substitute), which involves arbitrary forcing. The disagreement about the reading of «خَطِيْئاتِهم» was given in al-Aʿrāf. Abū Rajāʾ read «خَطِيَّاتهم» as a sound plural, except that he assimilated the yāʾ into the yāʾ that had been changed from the hamza. al-Jaḥdarī, and it is also transmitted from Ubayy, read «خطيئتِهم» in the singular with hamza. ʿAbd Allāh read «مِنْ خطيئاتِهم ما أُغْرِقوا», placing the redundant «ما» between the verb and what is attached to it. «مِنْ» is causal and is attached to «أُغْرِقوا». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "it marks the beginning of the range," which is not clear. The majority read «أُغرِقوا» from «أَغْرق». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «غُرِّقوا» with shadda; both are for making transitive. One says: «أغرَقْتُ زيداً في الماء» and «غَرَّقْتُه فيه».
His saying: {فَأُدْخِلُواْ}: it may be an expression of the future by the past, because its occurrence is certain, like {أتى أَمْرُ الله} [al-Naḥl: 1]; or it may be in its proper sense, what is meant being their being exposed to the Fire in their graves, as He says of the family of Pharaoh: {النار يُعْرَضُونَ عَلَيْهَا غُدُوّاً وَعَشِيّاً} [Ghāfir: 46].

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {دَيَّاراً}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "دَيَّار is among the nouns used in general negation. One says «ما بالدار دَيَّارٌ ودَيُّورٌ» ("there is no one at all in the house"), like قَيَّام and قَيُّوم. It is of the pattern فَيْعال from الدُّور or from الدار. Its origin is دَيْوار, and what is done to the origin of سَيِّد and مَيِّت was done to it; had it been فَعَّال, it would have been دَوَّاراً." End of quotation. He means that its wāw should have remained sound and not been changed to yāʾ. This is similar to the discussion he gave earlier of «متحيِّز», that its origin is مُتَحَيْوِز, of the pattern مُتَفَيْعِل, not مُتَفَعِّل, since otherwise it would have had to be مُتَحَوِّزاً, because it is from الحَوْز. It is also said in it دَوَّار, like قَيَّام and قَوَّام.
Makkī said: "Its origin is دَيْوار, then they assimilated the wāw into the yāʾ, like «مَيِّت», whose origin is مَيْوِت, then they assimilated the second into the first. It is also possible that they changed the wāw into yāʾ, then assimilated the first yāʾ into the second." I say: his saying "they assimilated the second into the first" is not permissible, since the established rule for two close letters is to change the first to the second, and the reverse is not allowed except as an anomaly or by a morphological necessity. As for the anomaly, it is like the reading «واذكر» [Yūsuf: 45] with dhāl and «فَهَلْ مِن مُّذَّكِرٍ» [al-Qamar: 15], also with dhāl; its investigation has already been given. As for the morphological necessity, it is like «امدحْ هِلالاً», with the hāʾ changed to ḥāʾ so that the stronger is not assimilated into the weaker; this is known to one who has worked in morphology (taṣrīf).

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {رَّبِّ اغفر لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ}: The majority read the dāl with fatḥa, as the dual of «والِد», meaning his two parents. al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with them both, Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmur and al-Nakhaʿī read «ولوَلَدَيَّ», the dual of «وَلَد», meaning his two sons Sām and Ḥām. Ibn Jubayr and al-Jaḥdarī read «ولوالِدِيْ» with kasra on the dāl, meaning his father. It is possible that he meant his nearest father, who begot him, and singled him out for mention because he is more honourable than the mother; or that he meant all who begot him, from Adam, peace be upon him, down to the one who begot him. «مؤمناً» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «تَباراً» is a second object; and the exception is a "voided" one (istithnāʾ mufarragh). التبار means destruction, and its origin is from breaking and crumbling. The investigation of that has already been given, and to Allah belong praise and favour.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا نُوحًا إِلَى قَوْمِهِ أَنْ أَنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ).
The words of the Exalted (أَنْ أَنْذِرْ): «أَنْ» may be in the sense of «أَيْ» (explicative, "that is"), or it may be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun); parallels to it have already been discussed.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ (١٥)).
(طِبَاقًا) has been discussed in al-Mulk.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا (١٧)).
(نَبَاتًا) is a noun standing for the maṣdar (ism al-maṣdar), so it occupies the place of «إِنْبَات», «نَبْت» and «تَنْبِيت». It is also said that the implied form is: «فَنَبَتُّمْ نَبَاتًا» (so you grew a growing).

ukberi-tibyan:20-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِتَسْلُكُوا مِنْهَا سُبُلًا فِجَاجًا (٢٠)).
(مِنْهَا) may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «تَسْلُكُوا», or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:22-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَكَرُوا مَكْرًا كُبَّارًا (٢٢) وَقَالُوا لَا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا (٢٣)).
(كُبَّارًا) is read with a doubled bāʾ and with a single one, meaning «كَبِير» (great). (وَدًّا) is read with a ḍamma and with a fatḥa; these are two dialectal forms. As for «يَغُوثَ» and «يَعُوقَ», they are diptotes (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf) because of the verb pattern and definiteness, though some declined them fully on the view that they are indefinite.

ukberi-tibyan:25-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مِمَّا خَطِيئَاتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا فَأُدْخِلُوا نَارًا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْصَارًا (٢٥) وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ دَيَّارًا (٢٦)).
The words of the Exalted (مِمَّا خَطِيئَاتِهِمْ): «مَا» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. because of their sins «أُغْرِقُوا» (they were drowned). The root form of (دَيَّارًا) is «دَيْوَار», because it is on the pattern «فَيْعَال», from «دَارَ يَدُورُ» (to turn, go round); then assimilation (idghām) took place.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Nūḥ
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿إنّا أرْسَلْنا نُوحًا إلى قَوْمِهِ أنْ أنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَأْتِيَهم عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾ ("Indeed, We sent Noah to his people: Warn your people before a painful punishment comes to them"). «أنْ» is in the position of an accusative by «أرْسَلْنا», because the original is «بِأنْ أنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ» ("with: warn your people"); when the bāʾ was dropped, the verb reached «أنْ» and put it in the accusative (accusative by removal of the preposition). Some people whose knowledge is approved said that the position of the like of it is genitive even though the bāʾ has dropped, because with «أنْ» the dropping of the bāʾ is acceptable, whereas the bāʾ is not dropped from the maṣdar (verbal noun): if you said «إنِّي أرْسَلْتُكَ بِالإنْذارِ والتَّهَدُّدِ» ("I sent you with warning and threatening"), it would not be permissible to say «إنِّي أرْسَلْتُكَ الإنْذارَ والتَّهَدُّدَ»; but if you said «إنِّي أرْسَلْتُكَ بِأنْ تُنْذِرَ وأنْ تُهَدِّدَ», then «إنِّي أرْسَلْتُكَ أنْ تُنْذِرَ وأنْ تُهَدِّدَ» would be permissible. The root meaning of «الإنْذار» in the language is informing of something to be feared, so that one is wary of it and does not expose oneself to it. It is also possible that «أنْ» is explicative (tafsīriyya) of what he was sent with, so the meaning would be: "Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, namely: warn your people."

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿يُرْسِلِ السَّماءَ عَلَيْكم مِدْرارًا﴾ ("He will send the sky upon you in abundant showers"). It was said that they had suffered drought, so he informed them that their belief in Allah would bring them, together with an ample share in the Hereafter, fertility and wealth in this world. ﴿مِدْرارًا﴾: abundant in flow, i.e. abundant in rain.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
﴿وَيُمْدِدْكم بِأمْوالٍ وبَنِينَ﴾ ("and give you increase in wealth and sons"): He will give you the adornment of this world, which is wealth and sons.
﴿وَيَجْعَلْ لَكم جَنّاتٍ﴾ ("and provide for you gardens"), i.e. orchards.

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ما لَكم لا تَرْجُونَ لِلَّهِ وقارًا﴾ ("What is the matter with you that you do not hope for waqār from Allah?"). It was said: "What is the matter with you that you do not fear the majesty of Allah?!" And it was said: "You do not hope for an outcome." Its true sense — and Allah knows best — is: what is the matter with you that you do not hope for the outcome of faith and so affirm the oneness of Allah, when He has placed for you in yourselves a sign pointing to His oneness — His creating you, and His creating the heavens and the earths, the sun and the moon? So He said: ﴿وَقَدْ خَلَقَكم أطْوارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 14] ("while He has created you in stages"), i.e. stage after stage: He moved you from state to state and from one aspect of creation to another. He created you from dust, then from a drop of sperm, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh; then He made the lump bone and clothed the bone with flesh.

zajjaj:15-15.t: Then He made them acknowledge, saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ طِباقًا﴾ ("Do you not see how Allah created seven heavens in layers?"). ﴿طِباقًا﴾ is accusative on two lines: one of them is "corresponding in layers (muṭābaqatan ṭibāqan)" [i.e. as a maṣdar]; the other is as a naʿt (adjective) of «سَبْعَ», i.e. "He created seven possessing layers."

zajjaj:16-16.t:
﴿وَجَعَلَ القَمَرَ فِيهِنَّ نُورًا﴾ ("and made the moon therein a light"). The scholars of Arabic said: it may be [that the moon is] in the lowest heaven, and ﴿فِيهِنَّ﴾ ("in them") was said because they are like a single thing. It has come in the exegesis that the face of the sun shines for the people of the earth from its back and its nape, and it shines for the people of the heavens; and likewise the moon.
[Translator's note: the source reads «يُضِيءُ لِأهْلِ الأرْضِ مِن ظَهْرِها، وقَفاها»; the usual form of this report is that its face shines for the people of the heavens and its back for the people of the earth, so the text may be disturbed. Translated as written.]

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿واللَّهُ أنْبَتَكم مِنَ الأرْضِ نَباتًا﴾ ("And Allah has caused you to grow from the earth a growth"): ﴿نَباتًا﴾ is construed, as a maṣdar (verbal noun), according to the meaning, because the meaning of «أنْبَتَكُمْ» is "He made you grow a growth (nabātan)". [Using] the maṣdar on the wording "He caused you to grow a causing-to-grow (inbātan)" and "a growth (nabātan)" — [the latter] is more eloquent in meaning.
[Translator's note: the final sentence is elliptical in the Arabic («والمَصْدَرُ عَلى لَفْظِ "أنْبَتَكم إنْباتًا، ونَباتًا"، أبْلَغُ في المَعْنى»); the bracketed words reflect one reading of it.]

zajjaj:2-3.t: ﴿قالَ يا قَوْمِ إنِّي لَكم نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ ﴿أنِ اعْبُدُوا اللَّهَ واتَّقُوهُ وأطِيعُونِ﴾ ("He said: O my people, I am to you a clear warner, [saying]: Worship Allah, fear Him and obey me"). Allah sent Noah and all the prophets with the command to worship Him, to prefer fearing Him, and to obey His messengers.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿لِتَسْلُكُوا مِنها سُبُلا فِجاجًا﴾ ("that you may follow therein broad roads"), i.e. clear paths.

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿وَوَلَدُهُ﴾ ("and his children"); it is also read «وَوُلْدُهُ». «الوَلَد» and «الوُلْد» have the same meaning, like «العَرَب» and «العُرْب», «العَجَم» and «العُجْم».

zajjaj:22-22.t: His saying ﴿وَمَكَرُوا مَكْرًا كُبّارًا﴾ ("And they plotted a tremendous plot"): one says «مَكْرٌ كَبِيرٌ», «كُبّارٌ» and «كِبّارٌ» with one meaning.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
﴿وَقالُوا لا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكم ولا تَذَرُنَّ ودًّا ولا سُواعًا﴾ ("And they said: Never leave your gods, and never leave Wadd, nor Suwāʿ"); it was also read «وُدًّا» with ḍamma on the wāw; ﴿وَلا يَغُوثَ ويَعُوقَ ونَسْرًا﴾ ("nor Yaghūth, Yaʿūq and Nasr"). These are five idols that existed among the people of Noah, which they worshipped; then they passed to the Arabs.
Wadd belonged to Kalb, Suwāʿ belonged to Hamdān, Yaghūth belonged to Madhḥij, and Nasr belonged to Ḥimyar.
[Translator's note: the source does not mention which tribe Yaʿūq belonged to, although it speaks of five idols.]
It was also read «يَغُوثًا ويَعُوقًا». «يَغُوث» and «يَعُوق» are diptotes (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), because they are on the pattern of a verb and they are definite. The reading which the readers and the Muṣḥaf follow is without nunation (tark al-ṣarf), and there is no alif in «يَغُوثَ» and «يَعُوقَ» in the written text; therefore it should only be read without nunation. Those who gave them nunation treated these two names as mostly declinable, since for them the basic state of nouns is declinability; or they treated them as indefinite even though they are definite, as though they said: "and never leave any idol of your idols". It should not be read so, because it contradicts the Muṣḥaf.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying: ﴿مِمّا خَطِيئاتِهِمْ﴾ ("Because of their sins"); it is also read «مِمّا خَطاياهُمْ». «خَطِيئَة» has the plurals «خَطايا» and «خَطِيئات». We have explained that earlier in the book.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿وَقالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ لا تَذَرْ عَلى الأرْضِ مِنَ الكافِرِينَ دَيّارًا﴾ ("And Noah said: My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any inhabitant from among the unbelievers"). «دَيّارًا» has the meaning of «أحَدًا» ("anyone"); one says «ما في الدّارِ أحَدٌ، وما بِها دَيّارٌ» ("there is no one in the house, there is no inhabitant in it"). Its original form is «دَيْوار», on the pattern fayʿāl; the wāw was changed into yāʾ, and one was assimilated into the other. Noah (peace be upon him) invoked against them only because Allah, Majestic and Exalted, revealed to him ﴿أنَّهُ لَنْ يُؤْمِنَ مِن قَوْمِكَ إلا مَن قَدْ آمَنَ﴾ [Hūd: 36] ("that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed").

zajjaj:28-28.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَلِمَن دَخَلَ بَيْتِيَ مُؤْمِنًا﴾ ("and whoever enters my house a believer"): they said «بَيْتِيَ» means "my place of prayer (masjid)". If you wish, you may make the yāʾ quiescent, and if you wish, you may give it fatḥa.
And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَزِدِ الظّالِمِينَ إلا تَبارًا﴾ ("and do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction"): its meaning — "except in tabār": «التَّبار» is destruction. Everything destroyed has been «تُبِّرَ»; therefore everything broken up is called «تِبْر».

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿يَغْفِرْ لَكم مِن ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ ("He will forgive you of your sins"): «يَغْفِرْ» is jussive (majzūm), the answer to the imperative: "Worship Allah, fear Him and obey me — He will forgive you of your sins." All the Basran grammarians — except Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ — do not assimilate the rāʾ into the lām; they do not permit «يَغْفِر لَّكُمْ». Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ holds the assimilation to be permissible. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh held that the rāʾ is a trilled (mukarrar) letter: whenever it is assimilated into the lām, its trill is lost and the letter is impaired. What is heard from the Arabs, and what the readers read, is pronouncing the rāʾ distinctly. The meaning of ﴿مِن ذُنُوبِكُمْ﴾ here is: "He will forgive you your sins"; «مِن» came in to single out the sins from all other things, not to make the sins partial. Similar to it is His saying ﴿فاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الأوْثانِ﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 30] ("So avoid the filth of idols"), meaning: avoid the filth which is the idols; the filth here is not some of the idols.
And His saying: ﴿وَيُؤَخِّرْكم إلى أجَلٍ مُسَمًّى إنَّ أجَلَ اللَّهِ إذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ﴾ ("and He will defer you to a specified term; indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, is not deferred") means: fear Allah and obey me, and He will defer you from the punishment, i.e. He will defer you so that you die other than by the death of those uprooted by punishment. Then He said: ﴿إنَّ أجَلَ اللَّهِ إذا جاءَ لا يُؤَخَّرُ﴾, meaning: when the term of death comes it is not deferred, whether by punishment or by uprooting.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿جَعَلُوا أصابِعَهم في آذانِهِمْ واسْتَغْشَوْا ثِيابَهُمْ﴾ ("they put their fingers in their ears and covered themselves with their garments"): it was said that they used to stop up their ears and cover their faces so as not to hear his words, and to go to extremes in turning away from him by covering their faces.
And His saying: ﴿وَأصَرُّوا﴾ ("and they persisted"): they persisted and had no intention of repenting of it. ﴿واسْتَكْبَرُوا﴾ ("and they were arrogant"): pride kept them from following Noah. The evidence for that is His saying: ﴿أنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ واتَّبَعَكَ الأرْذَلُونَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 111] ("Shall we believe you while the lowest follow you?").

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿إنِّي دَعَوْتُهم جِهارًا﴾ ("Then I called them openly"), i.e. I called them, making the call manifest to them. «جِهارًا» is accusative: a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "I called them, being open in calling to the oneness of Allah and fear of Him."

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إنِّي أعْلَنْتُ لَهم وأسْرَرْتُ لَهم إسْرارًا﴾ ("Then I announced to them publicly and confided to them secretly"), i.e. I mixed for them calling them in public with calling in secret. ﴿فَقُلْتُ اسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّكم إنَّهُ كانَ غَفّارًا﴾ [Nūḥ: 10] ("And I said: Ask forgiveness of your Lord; indeed, He is ever Forgiving"), i.e. seek your Lord's forgiveness.
